entries.tip: Never withhold a result to bait a counterclaim. Sheriffs, Surveyors and other investigators: post your role, target and exact result in your first speech after getting it, or the moment someone asks, and keep your last will current. Withholding protects nothing, since the Yakuza don't need your result to kill you, and it invites a trial. If someone else claims your role or exact result, counterclaim at once with your full log. Never vote against your own information to 'wait and see'. If you must vote in a way that looks odd, explain why during that trial. A result held back and revealed after an opponent's claim looks retrofitted, and a hidden investigator who votes with the Yakuza looks exactly like a fake.

entries.tip: Assume the real holder of any role you fake-claim is alive and will counterclaim, that an Accountant can audit your exact token count, that an exact-role check (Oracle, Ritualist, Diviner, Archivist or Surveyor list) can rule your claimed role out, and that a public role list plus flips can leave no slot for it. Never claim a Unique role whose holder may be alive. Never copy a role whose actions were already public (e.g. a Prosecutor): the real holder will counterclaim with earlier reads and correct night labels. Never fake-claim a role that has just been revealed on a flip, above all on the victim you visited. Pick a fake role whose tokens match yours: claim a tokenless role only if you hold no tokens. Never volunteer your token history or report more results than the role's tokens allow. A no-action claim is unsafe if you visited a target someone may have watched, so prepare a story that fits a token check or visit report. Visit results include Lookout and Tracker logs, Scout and Cartographer groups and FT counts. If you fake a visiting role (Tracker, Lookout), name your real visit destinations as your targets so these results can only confirm you, and fix the claim in night chat before you need it. Never improvise targets. If your claim is broken, don't switch to another power role a living player can counterclaim.

entries.tip: Keep your votes consistent with your stated reads. If you change your mind, say why before the vote; an unexplained switch gets cited against you. Village: a read/vote mismatch is a weak lead, not a verdict, because confused townies mismatch often. Check it against claims, mechanical results and PM links. Never shoot or hang on a mismatch alone. Never hang a credible power role (e.g. a Veteran whose alerts killed visitors) over an old Yes on a nomination: a Yes only opens a trial. When a group pushes a mismatch case, count whether its Guilty votes alone could decide the trial, and ask who benefits.

entries.tip: Dying with unused tokens is the usual Vigilante failure: holding all your shots makes you a Vanilla Villager. Shoot on a lead, not on proof. Set a concrete trigger by Day 2-3 and fire a Basic shot (1 token) once it's met, and fire anyway by the time the Yakuza could be near parity. Good leads include a claim conflict, an Evil check against an unverifiable claim, a credible map or group result that leaves one unconfirmed member as the likely holder, or a proven Yakuza's vote record or PM partners (e.g. the few who voted No on their nomination or argued to delay their hang). When roles are hidden on death and hard leads are scarce, the strongest claimless voice is a fair target: someone who leads nominations on 'silence' or always echoes the consensus without results. A lone read/vote mismatch or one player's private request is not enough on its own; bring a PM'd request into public first. If you hit a hidden Cardinal, the curse Divine-attacks a random Good player. A Basic shot that fails on a suspect no credible Medic protects is evidence of innate Defense (Arsonist or Serial Killer Standard, Jester or Executioner Basic), so post it the next Day. If you already suspect a Neutral killer and want the kill, only a Strong shot (3 tokens) beats Standard Defense. Claim only once your shots have paid off.

history.old: Hold your shots until you have a mechanical lead: a claim conflict, a flipped Yakuza's vote or PM partners, or votes that clearly contradict the player's own stated reads. entries.tip: A visit shows a destination, not an action or alignment. A track or watch cannot tell protection from framing or a Katana attack. A Lookout sees only visitors to their target, so watching the Katana holder shows nothing about the holder's attack. Killing an attacker at night does not cancel their attack that same night. A Lookout never sees their own visit, but that only matters if the Lookout could be the holder. If the Lookout has independent support (a Tracker confirms their visits, or earlier reports checked out) and X is the only other visitor to a Katana victim, treat it as near-proof against X. The same applies when several visitors are named and all but X have confirmed harmless explanations: X is then the lone unexplained visitor. This holds even more when X first denied the visit, claims a role that doesn't fit, or was the sole visitor to victims on several nights. Don't let 'a visit isn't an attack' or the self-visit caveat acquit such a visitor.

entries.tip: Don't defend a doomed teammate. Ballots are secret, but the totals are announced, and the town compares them with what everyone said. A hidden defensive vote still shows up as an extra No or Innocent, and your public defense is remembered after the teammate flips. Do the vote math in night chat first. If the team's No and Innocent votes (plus a Ballot Stuffer's doubled vote) can stop the execution, defend them: an exposed teammate saved beats a clean record. Otherwise vote Yes and Guilty with the town and say so. Plan the whole team's votes and stated positions across trials in advance. A doomed member's last words shouldn't defend or attack anyone in a way that maps back to teammates. The bus rule is for teammates only. If the nominee is a non-teammate who is likely a Jester, don't all vote Guilty: every Guilty vote is a ticket in the revenge draw, so some of you should vote Innocent.

entries.tip: Weigh contradictions between a player's own accepted premises or claimed knowledge far above awkward wording or delays. Investigators should still post results publicly once they matter, not only in a will that may come too late. When a Ritualist may be alive, never name another living player's exact role in your will or in public; write 'one of X/Y holds info, ask them'.

entries.tip: After a Yakuza flips, your top suspects are those who argued to delay or stop their hang, defended them, or exchanged PMs with them. Ballots are secret, so before each nomination and trial vote, ask every player to state their vote publicly. Then compare the stated votes with the announced totals: extra No or Innocent votes mean someone hid a defensive vote. Do the vote math first. An Innocent bloc that couldn't change a settled result proves little, and Yakuza will reuse it to steer suspicion onto townies. Pushing No or delay at the nomination, then Guilty once the hang is certain, is the more telling pattern. A stated Guilty vote on a flipped Yakuza clears no one. A bloc is a lead, not a verdict: a hidden investigator voting on their own info fits the same pattern, so demand a claim and results before hanging. Once every Yakuza has flipped and the game goes on, vote links to them mostly point at Neutrals who voted alongside them, and a Jester wants exactly that hang. Switch to who could have made the Neutral kills (douse or attack visits), and press for claims. If you hang a likely Jester anyway, keep the Guilty votes to a bare majority.

entries.tip: Treat the nomination and trial votes as separate decisions, unless a Clerk may hold an unused rig token. In that case a passed nomination can mean execution whatever the trial vote: vote Yes only on someone you'd accept dying, and vote No at the nomination if you are a likely target. At low player counts, don't vote Yes just to 'hear a defense'. The nominator's Yes is automatic, so don't read it as a stance. Before voting Guilty, name one concrete contradiction or mechanical fit in their claims, votes or results, and say why an innocent explanation no longer fits. A missing result or announcement that a role-block fully explains (a blocked prosecution, an empty investigation, 'no named target') is never a contradiction; check the rules before calling one. A contradiction doesn't separate a Yakuza from a Jester who wants the hang. If the nominee self-nominated, asked for the rope, or the case rests only on behaviour (vote-steering, PMs), run the Jester check first (t91), and don't let a recited 'contradiction' stand in for a mechanical case. Each of these counts as a mechanical case: an unexplained Evil result against a Vanilla claim; a denial reversed into a role claim; a group result (survey, census, map, archive slot math) whose other members are confirmed, so elimination names the remaining player; a corroborated lone visitor to a Katana victim whose claim doesn't fit; a visit count that leaves room for only one visitor on a Katana night; slot math plus matching blocks plus a refusal to claim any role. Such a case plus the suspect's refusal to answer a plain yes/no about their own visit or role is enough. A bare denial offered only once cornered on trial does not answer it. 'A dodge isn't a contradiction', 'name a contradiction in my posts' and 'what exact fact has been disproved?' must not shield them. The standard is a better explanation, not proof. If you said you would vote Guilty unless they answered and they didn't, vote Guilty. Never pad a case with a fact you haven't checked: one false detail lets the defense discredit the whole push. An Evil result explained only by an uncheckable claim (Ex-Con) is not a clean acquittal: test it before trusting it. Echoed concerns and corrected slips are not new evidence. Three Innocent trials end the Day with no hang, so give your trials to the strongest mechanical cases and convict on them.

entries.tip: Investigators (Sheriff, Lookout, Tracker) and protectors (Medic): never announce tonight's target in public or by private message. An announced target tells the Pharmacist whom to block and tells the Katana where to strike or what to avoid. Even a PM whose contents stay hidden marks you: everyone sees that it was sent, and Yakuza read a PM from one claimed investigator to another as a sign that both are worth killing. This covers only tonight's planned target. Once a result exists, post it in full (night, target, exact result) at once. Never stretch secrecy into withholding or vaguening a past result, and never invent a mechanical excuse for it: Astral actions like an Oracle guess can't be seen by anyone. Exception: a Trapper's announced trap works as a deterrent, because killers avoid the trapped player (see the Trapper entries).

entries.tip: Map who starts PM clusters and who co-nominates. If the same few players DM each other early and then push the same nomination with no new information, treat them as a likely Yakuza bloc, and once one of them flips, use the shared vote record against the others. But a PM link is a lead, never a hang on its own. A Jester or Executioner leaves PM trails on purpose: one player privately asking several others for Yes votes, or a lone Day 1 PM to a later-flipped Yakuza, fits a Neutral as well as a Yakuza. Ask what they verified, and judge the target on their own results, not on who pushes. A villager PMing for votes on a credible result (a Lookout log) is pushing clumsily, not proving a bloc, and Yakuza will reframe it as a 'whip' to hang them. Before hanging on a PM link, require votes or a mechanical result that needs them to be a teammate.

entries.tip: Save the forge token for a night your target is actually likely to die (e.g. the Katana target when no protector is suspected). The victim's true role is revealed with the will, so never give a forged will a specific role claim you haven't confirmed: a mismatch proves a Fabricator exists and voids the will's accusation (and exposes the frame). Forge something vague that fits many roles, or wait for a victim whose role you've worked out. A forged will must fit the public transcript, and invented chronology others can check exposes you. Don't spend a frame on someone who already reads Evil (Jester, Executioner, Ex-Con). Never put a fake role in your own will that your death reveal will disprove; it also discredits teammates making the same claim.

entries.tip: Survival alone confirms nothing. A power-role claimant who survives a Katana attack may be real, since Evil rarely spends its Katana on a fake, but Arsonists and Serial Killers have innate Standard Defense that stops the Katana, and Jesters and Executioners have Basic Defense. Ask the survivor at once for one claim that explains their Defense (e.g. a Medic token self-protection, or a named protector). If no credible Medic claims the save, keep innate-Defense Neutrals in the pool and check the claim against token audits and visit logs. A survivor who first says 'innate Defense' or 'nobody protected me' and later claims Medic is far more likely a Neutral killer than a protected investigator. Role-blocks are different: only the blocked player is told, so 'I was blocked' is the claimant's own word and verifies nothing by itself. But it fully explains a missing result, so never treat that gap as a lie. Test the claim with an audit or a Lookout instead, and weigh repeated blocks reported before anyone pressed the claimant as mild support.

entries.tip: Get the mechanics right before calling something a contradiction. Night actions are optional unless a role says 'must'. Two players can claim the same role unless the rules make it unique, or unless a role list plus flips accounts for every player: once every unshown slot is filled by a flip, a role listed once exists exactly once, and a second claimant is a provable liar. But 'roles can repeat' only means a claim isn't disproved; it is not evidence for it. A claim of the exact role that just flipped dead, made by a player seen visiting that victim, is still close to a confession: weigh it with the other evidence and don't acquit on the bare possibility. Count living players and elapsed nights as of the right moment: on Day 2 only Night 1 has passed, so 'name the night of your result' is not a contradiction, and demanding it repeatedly only creates false certainty. A false 'contradiction' costs the accuser credibility, and a real one dismissed as 'roles aren't unique' frees a Yakuza.

entries.tip: An archive or partial survey is a sample, not a census. It shows that roles exist, never how many. Never say a duplicate claim 'proves' a liar. Say instead that it shifts the odds, e.g. 'only 5 of 7 roles were sampled, so three Vanilla claims against one listed Vanilla are worth testing'. Overstating the math gets a correct suspicion discredited and the trial acquitted. Once a list is public, keep a role inventory every Day and post it. The list is one claimant's report until something corroborates it. Of the N roles shown, floor(0.75*N) are real and the rest are fakes that may or may not be in the game. So a listed role may be absent, and a role listed once may have an unsampled second holder. Use slot math to decide whom to press for an exact claim and whom to audit, watch or guess. Then hang on the contradiction that test produces (e.g. a token count against a Vanilla claim, an Evil check), not on slot math alone. Roles proven by public effects (a prosecution proves a Prosecutor, a clean a Mortician, an ignite an Arsonist) are certain. Track Unique roles (Smuggler, Vulture) separately: once one is proven, every other living claimant of it is a proven liar. A claim made right after a result that only explains that result is not placed, so keep it open. When the inventory narrows to a few unclaimed players, demand an exact claim from each; a refusal then is heavy evidence. Late in the game an unverified 'Vanilla' claim is worth testing early. Keep deductions conditional: corroborating one entry doesn't verify the whole list.

entries.tip: Stay quiet and never hint publicly that a Wiretap exists. The Village's own fear of a Wiretap often shuts down PM evidence for you. Never quote or closely paraphrase a PM: a quote proves you read it, and the two people in that exchange will ask how. Use what you read to steer votes and your team's night choices without revealing content. If you must use it, have an Eavesdropper cover ready with a named previous-night target who took part in that exchange (see t119). Hold the Katana yourself when the team needs a low-value holder.

entries.tip: Fortune Teller numbers are unordered: one counts distinct players visited, the other counts distinct players who visited anyone. Every visiting action counts, including Lookout watches, Tracker tracks, Accountant audits, Medic protections, Fabricator frames and the Katana. Self-visits count in both. A Veteran's alert isn't a visit, but anyone who visits the Veteran is. Blocked and Astral actions (Oracle, Ritualist, ignite, map) count in neither. Players who died that night still count. Only a Katana holder who also uses their own visiting action can add a second destination, so visited <= visitors + 1; if the numbers differ by 2 or more, the larger one is visitors. Read small counts literally. On a night with a Katana death, a visitor total of 1 means the holder made every visit that night. Anyone who claims a visit that night is then the holder or is lying, and a player who refuses to state their night action, or gives only a bare denial, is the hang. A totals-only role can't name visitors, so 'the FT's visitors are unnamed' is not a flaw, and evil uses that line to hang a real FT. FT: line your totals up publicly against every claimed visit, then ask each player with no claimed action for a plain yes/no on the leftover visit. A total that doesn't fit shows that some set of claims is false, not which claim. List every account that repairs it (holder acting twice, Ex-Con random visit, douses, switched plans). Outside the one-visitor case, never hang on the count alone, least of all against an exact-role check or a flip. Ask for the raw totals per night and the derivation before calling a count a lie.

entries.tip: (Yakuza) Use one-shot Day tokens (Clerk rig, puppet, Mortician clean) early, on the first Day they can swing a vote, and before their holder is exposed. Don't wait for a 'decisive day': holders who keep saving them die with them unused. Combine them when you can. Rig so that any nomination you can pass kills a Villager, puppet a trusted villager to push it, and kill and clean the puppet that night so their will can't expose it. Once you hold a voting majority, stop arguing and vote as a bloc, and hang the most dangerous town role first (e.g. a Veteran). A puppet lapses if you die the night you spend it (R21), so spend it at least a night before a likely death. Never rig a Day when you or a teammate is the likely nominee, because the rig executes your own side.

entries.tip: Accurate information proves access, not alignment. A Diviner can post real role results as a 'Surveyor', a Wiretap can quote real private messages as an 'Eavesdropper', and an evil player can truthfully expose a rival killer. A visiting killer can also present their own real visits (douses, a Katana hit) as 'Tracker' tracks, which then fit Fortune Teller counts and Cartographer groups perfectly. A fit with visit totals shows that the visits happened, not who made them or why. Before clearing an info claimer, ask which hostile role could produce the same evidence. Then look for a check that tells them apart: an Oracle guess, an Accountant audit, or a Lookout on the claimant's target. An exact-role result from an investigator with a proven record outweighs visit-count consistency. Confirming one detail authenticates only that detail. When such a claimer is exposed as hostile, re-examine everyone they cleared, but don't hang the subjects of their true reads just because they were 'confirmed' by them.

history.old: Survey-style or role results that keep matching claims and flips don't verify the claimer. A Yakuza Diviner publishes real reads on non-teammates and invents 'clears' for teammates. Trust only results that revealed something nobody had said yet, and require an independent check (Oracle guess, Accountant audit). When such a claimer flips Yakuza, re-examine everyone they cleared, but don't hang their true reads' subjects just for being 'confirmed' by them.
history.note: Bob (Diviner) posed as Surveyor and Heidi (Wiretap) quoted real PMs as an 'Eavesdropper'. Alice, Carol, Dave, Erin, Grace, Ivan, Mallory, Niaj and Olivia all made this point.

history.old: Accurate information proves access, not alignment. A Diviner can post real role results as a 'Surveyor', a Wiretap can quote real private messages as an 'Eavesdropper', and an evil player can truthfully expose a rival killer. Before clearing an info claimer, ask which hostile role could produce the same evidence. Then look for a check that tells them apart: an Oracle guess, an Accountant audit, or visit totals. Confirming one detail authenticates only that detail. When such a claimer flips Yakuza, re-examine everyone they cleared, but don't hang the subjects of their true reads just because they were 'confirmed' by them.
history.note: Moderator: Heidi's fake 'tracks' were her real douses. They fit Ivan's 2/2 and 2/3 and Alice's group of three, while Carol's correct Oracle result (Heidi is not a Tracker) was discounted. Also removes the reliance on role flips.

entries.tip: Fake-claim a role whose results look like yours, such as Surveyor. Divine teammates who must visit risky targets: Strong Defense stops traps and Vigilante shots, and the visit can be published as a fake survey. Mix in at least one harmless unconfirmable result so a Roleplayer fallback stays believable. Remember an Accountant sees you at 0 tokens, and a gifted token is thrown away.

support.note: Frank's Surveyor cover held three days and he divined Bob (the Katana holder) on N3. It broke to Erin's Oracle WRONG, and Grace's 0-token audit would have exposed it too.
Bob: a Diviner can imitate Surveyor results but not its token inventory. His later secret self-divine contradicted his claim of inactivity on Ivan's 6/4 count.
Moderator (0.4) and Grace (0.16): Alice published accurate groups pointed at Neutral and Village players, let Carol confirm a hit, and became the most trusted voice.

entries.tip: Audit the newest claimed token role (Surveyor, Philanthropist, Medic) and late Vanilla or unclaimed players early: Yakuza fake token roles to explain Diviner-style results, and Yakuza token roles (Clerk, Smuggler, Mortician) hide behind Vanilla. Work out the expected count first (start tokens, spends, gifts) so you can act on the result immediately. Don't announce the audit or PM the claimer. A Lookout who independently sees your visit makes the town trust your count.

support.note: Grace audited Frank to 0 tokens but was killed before she could report it.
Alice: work out expected totals first. Gifts and spent tokens change counts, so a total is a snapshot, not a role confirmation.
Alice's N2 audit of Niaj (1 token) was read as a resource count. It ruled out a tokenless Arsonist without being treated as a role check.
Bob and Ivan: Ivan's early audits of suspects gave the 2-token count that broke Carol's Party Animal claim and the 0 count that broke Erin's Veteran claim.
Erin and Ivan: audits of claimed token roles were cross-checked and held up as information.
Erin: a 0 on a tokenless claimant (Vanilla Dave) said little. Audit claimed token roles, where a 0 is a real lead.
Grace: a 0 on a tokenless claimant proved nothing; her 2-token audit on claimed Prosecutor Ivan was the decisive one but died with her.

history.old: Audit the newest claimed token role (Surveyor, Philanthropist, Medic) early; Yakuza fake token roles to explain Diviner-style results. Work out the expected count first (start tokens, spends, gifts) so you can act on the result immediately. Don't announce the audit or PM the claimer.
history.note: Moderator and Dave: Frank's audits of the late Vanilla claimants Mallory (1) and Carol (2), with Judy's watch confirming his visit, decided both hangs.

entries.tip: Guess the public role claims of suspicious or load-bearing players: trusted investigators, defenders of exposed Yakuza and cheap VV claims. A WRONG exposes a fake at once, and a RIGHT clears them. Confirming an already-harmless claim gains little. Post every result in one message the next Day: night, target, exact role guessed, RIGHT or WRONG (e.g. 'N4: guessed Heidi = Tracker, WRONG'). A bare 'X is not a Tracker' sounds evasive. Your guess is Astral, so no 'exposure' excuse applies. Give a stated reason with every nomination, argue for a Vigilante shot in public rather than by PM, and keep your planned next guess in your will. Once confirmed, assume you die tonight and keep your will hedged.

support.note: Erin's WRONG on Frank = Surveyor got Frank hanged as a Diviner. Her RIGHT on Niaj = Ex-Con gained little.
Moderator: Alice spent N1 confirming Frank's own Vanilla claim, which gained little. Her later Ex-Con guess on Carol was the valuable one but got blocked.
Mallory and Ivan: Mallory's exact guesses (Erin = Ex-Con, Frank = Jester) were verified and cleared her. She advises posting the exact guess and result early.
Frank and Erin: Carol's right Diviner guess on Grace drew the Katana the next night. Post exact results promptly so they outlive you.

history.old: Guess the public role claims of suspicious or load-bearing players: trusted investigators, defenders of flipped Yakuza and cheap VV claims. A WRONG exposes a fake at once, and a RIGHT clears them. Confirming an already-harmless claim gains little. Once confirmed, assume you die tonight and keep your will hedged.
history.note: Moderator: Carol's unexplained D3 nomination, her vague N4 result, a false exposure excuse and a private shoot request to Grace got a real Oracle hanged on D6. Her will's Arsonist plan later won the game.

entries.tip: Give tokens only to roles verified by something other than their own claim. Best is a role confirmed by flips whose token pays off by day, e.g. a Prosecutor whose targets flipped Yakuza. Never announce whom you plan to gift. You're never told if the token was thrown away, so a fake claimer can just 'confirm' the gift, and your credibility gets tied to theirs.

support.note: Ivan announced a survey token for Frank. Frank 'confirmed' it, and once Frank flipped Diviner, Ivan looked like his partner and was hanged.
Judy and Grace: the gift to a verified Prosecutor was decisive.
Niaj gave Mallory a medic token, and she died N4 with 3 unspent tokens. Niaj says verify which claimant is real before gifting.
Moderator: Erin gave both tokens to Surveyor Carol, whose claim was corroborated. The extra tokens funded surveys, and Carol's will confirming the gifts cleared Erin on D4.

history.old: Give tokens only to roles verified by something other than their own claim, and never announce whom you plan to gift. You're never told if the token was thrown away, so a fake claimer can just 'confirm' the gift, and your credibility gets tied to theirs.
history.note: Judy gifted Grace, whose two prosecutions had both flipped Yakuza, a token on N5. That token hanged Heidi on D7.

entries.tip: On trial, lead with one concrete, checkable alternative explanation of the evidence, e.g. the exact visit assignment that fits the numbers. A counter-accusation reads as deflection; a worked example that collapses the case can move votes.

support.note: Ivan's reflection on his hanging over FT counts.

entries.tip: Never narrow down your trap's location, in public or private ('not on X, Y'); a PM exchange with one player also hints the trap is there. You can't trap yourself, so once identified you're a safe kill. Stay unidentified as long as you can and let the trap's mere existence deter.

support.note: Mallory's exclusions let the Yakuza route kills around her trap. The trap only fired on the final night.

entries.tip: Track where a Trapper's trap could be: every visit that doesn't kill rules a player out, and the Trapper's PM partners are likely spots. Avoid visiting the likely trapped player, or have the Diviner give the holder Strong Defense, until the winning night. Night deaths are checked together, so a killing blow still wins even if the holder dies; give that last Katana to the least useful teammate.

support.note: Mallory's trap killed Alice on the final night, too late. Alice, Bob, Frank and Olivia all reported this.

entries.tip: Anyone fabricating a night account (Yakuza, Neutral killers) must test it against the global visit arithmetic, not just individual witnesses. Keep a ledger of claimed visitors, distinct destinations and token counts. Claiming protection on an already crowded target erases the extra destination your real kill created. Yakuza: choose the Katana holder so the night's visits match the team's public claims. A holder whose own action hits the kill target counts as one visitor.

support.note: Alice, Olivia and the moderator: the holders were chosen deliberately, and Judy's counts fit the Yakuza stories.

history.old: Against a Fortune Teller, choose the Katana holder so the night's visits match your team's public claims. A holder whose own action hits the kill target counts as one visitor. Plan the visitor and target counts each night; unexplained extras give the town 'hidden visitor' evidence.
history.note: Judy (SK) claimed Medic visits that hid her kill destinations, and Ivan's totals exposed her. Rupert, Heidi and Bob made the same point. Broadened from Yakuza to anyone faking a night account.

entries.tip: Don't vouch for other players in your last will unless something independent of their own claims verified them. A dead player's endorsement carries extra weight and props up a Yakuza.

support.note: Mallory's reflection on the trusted fake claims.

entries.tip: Estimate the Yakuza count early (about 3 in 11, 4 in 12-13) and count evil votes every day. Before each late-game hang, work out the worst case and how many more mis-hangs you can afford: if every unconfirmed Guilty voter could be Yakuza, a mis-hang may hand them the win. When one more wrong hang gives Evil the majority, nominate only from the remaining unconfirmed pool, never a player outside it over a self-admitted slip. Once the Yakuza are one night kill away from a majority (e.g. 4 of 7), everyone with information must post it now, before that night; results revealed after evil holds the votes are worthless. Near that line, spend the hang on the strongest Yakuza suspect rather than a Neutral killer, who doesn't add to the Yakuza vote.

Moderator: the D5 mis-hang of Dave at low count lost the game outright. The town should have spent the hang on the best-evidenced suspect, Bob.

Moderator and Grace: at 5 alive, a single vote decided every nomination. The Village didn't do the math and counted the Jester as a swing voter too late.
Moderator (0.4) and Bob (0.16): at 4 alive Judy hanged Arsonist Bob with Yakuza votes, leaving her alone against Erin and Heidi, and the Katana ended it N5.
Moderator: with two Yakuza votes in a 5-player trial, one Village Guilty decided Carol's hang. The town didn't count the votes first.

history.note: Moderator, Alice and Niaj: after Erin (SK) was hanged and Alice killed, the 4 Yakuza held 4 of 7 seats. Niaj posted 'Heidi visited Alice' on D4, too late, and the Yakuza hanged Bob and then Frank.

history.old: Estimate the Yakuza count early (about 4 in a 12-13 player game) and count evil votes every day. Before each late-game hang, count the worst case: if every unconfirmed Guilty voter could be Yakuza, a mis-hang may hand them the win. Once the Yakuza are one night kill away from a majority (e.g. 4 of 7), everyone with information must post it now, before that night; results revealed after evil holds the votes are worthless. Near that line, spend the hang on the strongest Yakuza suspect rather than a Neutral killer, who doesn't add to the Yakuza vote.
history.note: D6, 5 alive with 2 Yakuza: Dave was Oracle-confirmed, and Mallory said the Yakuza were among Frank, Grace and Judy. Dave hanged Mallory over her ballot slips instead, and the Yakuza won 2 of 3. Reported by the moderator and Mallory.

entries.tip: (Village) Jester warnings: suspect a Jester in a player who pushes hard with no evidence, self-nominates 'as a test', or makes a lone, easily disproved claim that contradicts a well-supported report and seems eager to be tried. A typical case is jumping onto a survey or archive pool's role so the real holder counterclaims. Track the conversion: if an archive lists Executioner and anyone has died at night, an Executioner whose target that was is now a Jester. An Evil Sheriff result on a Vanilla claimant with 0 tokens fits a Jester or Executioner as well as a Yakuza. A mild Day 1 dissent plus a lone PM to a later-flipped Yakuza doesn't rule a Jester out. A caught liar is a liar, not necessarily a Yakuza. If a more clearly Yakuza player is available, hang them first. Before any hang, ask whether the nominee wins by being hanged, and if so prefer to leave them alive. If you must hang, agree in public on a bare majority of Guilty votes and have everyone else vote Innocent. The revenge Divine-attacks a random Guilty voter, and no protection stops it. Confirmed power roles (Medic, investigators, a Prosecutor with tokens) must vote Innocent.

support.note: Moderator and Dave: Frank (Jester) pushed Carol all of D1, self-nominated on D2 and said 'if you want a real test, vote Guilty'. All 11 voted Guilty. The revenge happened to hit Mallory (Yakuza), but it could have hit Ivan or Bob.
Ivan: Heidi pushed for her own hanging, drew a unanimous Guilty vote, and her revenge killed Ivan.

Moderator, Judy, Erin, Dave, Grace: Grace became a Jester when her Executioner target Judy died to the N2 Katana. The town hanged her 9-1 on a broken Medic claim, and Erin, the real Medic, voted Guilty. The revenge killed Erin. The 'hurt' filings describe the town ignoring the tip.

Moderator: the town never hanged self-nominating Jester Frank despite many trials, and he lost.

Moderator: once Carol confirmed Judy as Jester and Dave as Executioner (later Jester), the Village refused every nomination of them. Neither Neutral won, and no revenge fired.
Moderator (0.4), Alice, Carol, Dave, Frank and Heidi (0.16 each): the Village refused Grace's Jester self-nomination 1-7 and never hanged her, so the Jester lost.

Moderator: Grace (Jester) fake-claimed Sheriff 'Dave Evil' with no visit on Alice's Lookout list and invited the nomination. Nobody raised the Jester possibility, she was hanged 10-0, won, and her revenge killed Ivan. Hanging a Jester gives them the win, and their revenge kills a random Guilty voter, who may be a key Village role. Before any hang, ask whether the nominee's win condition benefits from it.

entries.tip: Build a hard, Village-sounding case. A fake investigative counterclaim against a credible info role (e.g. a fake Tracker result contradicting a Lookout's list) is a fast route to a hang. Commit to it and reject the Roleplayer excuse the town offers. A self-nomination framed as a 'test' can also work, but repeated self-nominations or an open Jester claim make the town refuse to hang you.

Grace (won): she claimed the Medic role from Heidi's survey pool, the real Medic counterclaimed with a log, and the town hanged her 9-1.

Moderator and Frank: Frank self-nominated six times and asked Dave by PM for a Yes vote. Dave called it a Jester pattern on D1, the Oracle confirmed it, and no nomination of Frank got more than 4 Yes votes.
Frank: repeated self-nominations after his confessed lie drew Innocent votes from everyone. He suggests spreading the pressure through other players' nominations.
Frank: spamming self-nominations after a confessed fake claim drew No votes and wore down budget; pick one credible route early.
Grace: a fake Sheriff 'Evil' result that conflicted with a public Lookout list got her hanged 10-0 on D2, and she won.

history.note: Heidi (Jester, won): her fake Tracker result against Grace, plus refusing the Roleplayer escape, got her hanged 11-0.

entries.tip: Never flatly deny a night visit that a Lookout or Tracker could have seen. Agree on a plausible cover action in night chat before Day starts, and if a visit is exposed, admit it at once with that cover. A denial followed by a reversal is far more damning than the visit itself. Don't publicly endorse a Village player's account of a night when you visited the same target (e.g. backing a Medic's protection claim on your Katana target). A cover revealed later then reads as a second, invented claim.

Moderator, Alice, Frank, Mallory, Erin: Heidi's D3 denial of any N1-N2 action, then a Tracker claim on D4, was cited at every later trial and hanged her on D7.
Heidi: Bob answered the Erin visit question with 'I won't post my choices', and it hanged him. An agreed cover admitted at once would have fit the tip.

Grace, Mallory, Ivan and the moderator: Grace refused to name her N4 target, then flatly denied a visit the FT count implied, and was tried on D5. Ivan's admitted Erin visit matched Bob's log.
Moderator, Heidi: Heidi's flat N3-N4 no-visit denials were contradicted by the FT counts. She then skipped the N5 question and was hanged D6.
Moderator, Bob, Frank: Frank, claiming Vanilla, flatly denied the N5 visit to Grace that Bob had tracked. Alice's counts fit the track, and Frank was hanged 4-1 on D6.

entries.tip: Never announce your protection target, in public or by private message (a Wiretap reads PMs). Free Standard protection stops the Katana, so spend Strong tokens only when a Strong attack is credible (Serial Killer, Vigilante, Veteran, trap), on a confirmed investigator likely to be hit. Keep one token for a Standard self-protection: at 0 tokens you can't protect yourself. If a Pharmacist may be alive, don't protect the same claimed player in an obvious pattern.

history.old: Never announce your protection target, in public or by private message. Spend Strong tokens on the nights a confirmed investigator is most likely to be hit, because tokens unspent at death are wasted. If a Pharmacist may be alive, don't protect the same claimed player in an obvious pattern.
history.note: Niaj: Standard protection saved Olivia on N1 and Mallory on N2 against the Katana. He advised against spending tokens just because a target is important.

entries.tip: If a teammate is likely to be checked by a Sheriff tonight, give them the Katana so they read Good. This matters most on the night after they were nominated, tried or publicly suspected. An idle Grunt gains nothing by keeping it by default. Pair it with a block on the known protector. Weigh this against the visit risk if a Lookout or Tracker is active.

support.note: Moderator: Grace held the Katana on N3, read Not Evil to Carol and blocked Ivan, and the Katana killed Carol.
Niaj and Carol both advised moving the Katana to the teammate likely to be scanned. Erin's N1 and N2 checks caught Carol and Mallory, who weren't holding it.

history.old: If a teammate is likely to be checked by a Sheriff tonight (e.g. one under suspicion), consider giving them the Katana so they read Good. Pair it with a block on the known protector. Weigh this against the visit risk if a Lookout or Tracker is active.
history.note: Moderator (0.4) and Bob (0.16): Bob was tried on D3, but the Katana stayed on Grunt Erin on N3. Heidi checked Bob, got Evil, and he was hanged D4.

entries.tip: If the last known Yakuza dies and the game doesn't end, a Neutral is still alive. Count the players, check the Vulture threshold (max(floor(N/4),2)) and look hard at the weakest or latest claim. Don't hang a claimed Cardinal near the endgame: their death Divine-attacks a random Good player and can hand a Vulture the win.

support.note: Moderator and Dave: after Judy died the game continued. Heidi (Vulture) nominated Cardinal Erin, whose hang would have left 2 alive. Dave and Erin blocked it, and Heidi was hanged.
Olivia, Bob and Peggy: after all three Yakuza flipped and the game continued, the town forced claims and per-night ledgers, tracked the Vulture threshold and hanged Erin.

entries.tip: Claim a plausible role early, one an Oracle or other exact-role check can't easily falsify (not a bare Vanilla), and keep it. Never copy a role whose actions were already public or whose real holder may be among the unclaimed (e.g. a Prosecutor): they counterclaim with earlier reads and correct night labels. If someone fake-claims your Unique role, your flip exposes them: open a private deal with that player early, on the day they claim. Let others lead the pushes; avoid vouching for players early, lone Guilty votes and aggressive endgame nominations, especially of a Cardinal. Plan around the actual threshold of max(floor(N/4),2) alive at the start of a Day.

entries.tip: Judge a Roleplayer claim by its timing and consistency. A Roleplayer is told a fake investigative role and believes it: they claim that role from the start, never claim Vanilla, and never 'know' they are a Roleplayer. They can only suspect it, once their results clash with a flip or a confirmed claim. A real one flags the clash early, before others claim the slot, and pushes against other Roleplayer claimants. A Vanilla claim that later becomes Roleplayer, an 'I know I'm the Roleplayer', or a claim made only once cornered or prosecuted is almost certainly a lie. When two players claim the same investigative role and their results conflict, consider an honest Roleplayer before calling either one a liar. If an archive, profile or survey shows 'Roleplayer', the duplicate claim may need no Evil player at all. Discount the claimant with the odder, unverifiable result instead of spending the Day hanging them, keep the other claimant's results, and spend the hang on the unclaimed pool. Also be suspicious when 'blind' results land exactly on the night's kill victims or fit claims made that same day.

entries.tip: Delay-the-hang pitches ('tomorrow's test settles it, Innocent costs nothing', 'vote Innocent to expose a rig', 'no nomination before tonight's results') are classic Yakuza lines. Every night of delay gives the Katana a free kill, and when it kills an information role each night, the result you are waiting for usually dies with its holder. When a hang already has a mechanical basis, ignore rig-test pitches; the pusher is often the Clerk. Once a player is the best mechanical fit (named by slot math, fits the observed blocks or visits, refuses to claim a role), hang them that Day. Before granting a reprieve for a test, state which result would discriminate, what interference is likely, and what happens if the test doesn't occur. A blocked or missing check is no result, not a clearance. Ask whether the test resolves today's dispute; if not, hang the strongest case today.

entries.tip: Your claim is self-proving: the prosecution is announced the next Day, and Yakuza can't fake it. Stay unclaimed while your tokens are live. Spend each prosecution as soon as a solid mechanical lead exists, while enough Village voters are alive to win the trial. If you hold tokens for the endgame, the Katana removes your voters first and you may die with them unused. Good leads: a flipped Yakuza's slip or PM partner, a claim that overflows a public role list, a player in a confirmed visitor list, or a small Guilty bloc on a proven townie. Never spend one on a claimant whose results keep checking out (e.g. an Oracle with a verified hit). An acquittal wastes the token and one of the Day's three trials. A prosecution skips the nomination vote, so No votes can't stall it. Before each prosecution, name the target as a suspect in public that Day, but don't announce that you will prosecute tonight: a Pharmacist will block you. Log each prosecution in your will by NIGHT (N2, N3), not by trial day. If a copycat counterclaims, those earlier reads and correct labels are your proof. If you are role-blocked, you are told and no token is spent. Post 'N3: prosecution of X was role-blocked' in your first message the next Day, before anyone can call the missing trial a bluff, and ask an Accountant to confirm your token count. Under R21 the prosecution still fires even if you die that night, so spend your last token on your top suspect even when you expect to be killed.

entries.tip: (Party Animal) Choose blocks by the damage they prevent. Block the strongest Katana-holder suspect every night: a player a Lookout or Tracker saw at a victim, the last living name an elimination map allows, or late in the game the likeliest lone holder. Keep blocking that suspect every night until they are hanged. Switching away hands them a free kill, often on you. The Katana passes to a teammate when its holder dies, so re-check who likely holds it after every death. Before you have a suspect, use blocks as tests on claimed Vanillas and quiet players. A block that fails because the target can't be role-blocked shows an immune role (Pharmacist, Smuggler, Veteran or Party Animal). Post it with the moderator's exact wording. A no-kill night that matches your block is the town's strongest lead against a lone holder. Write each block target in your will and post it publicly the next Day, before anyone can confirm it. A target who later confirms being blocked proves you are real. Never block a protector or investigator confirmed by an independent source, and avoid blocking quiet players who defended confirmed claims, who may be a hidden Vigilante. A persistent liar who keeps showing no visits may be an Executioner, and blocking them prevents nothing.

In the endgame, block the likely Katana holder. Never block a protector or investigator confirmed by an independent source (Oracle, track, audit); that removes the town's own protection. A persistent liar who keeps showing no visits may be an Executioner, and blocking them prevents nothing.
history.note: Ivan blocked Lookout-exposed Mallory N2 (no kill) and Heidi N4 (no kill), posted the log, and Olivia's confirmation made it hang-worthy. Alice: the N3 block on unclaimed Vigilante Olivia wasted a night.

history.old: (Party Animal) Choose blocks by the damage they prevent. Block the strongest Katana-holder suspect every night: a player a Lookout or Tracker saw at a victim, or late in the game the likeliest lone holder. A no-kill night that matches your block is the town's strongest lead against a lone holder. Write each block target in your will and post it publicly the next Day, before anyone can confirm it; a target who later confirms being blocked proves you are real. Never block a protector or investigator confirmed by an independent source, and avoid blocking quiet players who defended confirmed claims, who may be a hidden Vigilante. A persistent liar who keeps showing no visits may be an Executioner, and blocking them prevents nothing.
history.note: Moderator and Grace: Grace's failed N2 block exposed Pharmacist Erin, and her N4 block on holder Frank stopped his attack on her. On N5 she blocked Alice instead, and Frank killed her.

entries.tip: Place traps for the next night's threat: a new trap is not armed on the night you place it, and replacing an armed trap resets that delay. Once you have a useful armed trap, consider leaving it in place. It persists through your death and through role-blocks on you.

support.note: Carol's reflection.
Grace: a new trap replaces the old one at once and arms only the next night. Astral actions don't trigger it.

entries.tip: Consult the archive early, while the living population and your sample are largest; waiting risks dying with the token unused. Report the full list, duplicates included, and remind the town how it is built. Of the N roles shown, floor(0.75*N) are real roles of random players, and the rest are fakes drawn from all roles. So any single entry may be fake, a missing role may be present, and a role shown once can have several holders. Read it as odds, not a census. A dangerous entry (Arsonist, Serial Killer) should start a hunt, not be dismissed as a likely fake. Cross the list with flips and confirmed claims after every death to narrow the rest.

support.note: Dave's reflection.
Bob, Frank, Heidi, Mallory all stressed that the anonymous sample proves roles exist, not who holds them.
Carol, Alice, Dave, Heidi and Frank (0.16 each): the archive must be read as odds, not a census. Carol's 'one Vanilla slot' misreading cost the Village a Day of credibility.

against.note: Bob: consulting on N1 left a list nobody could cross-check, and it was dismissed as unverifiable. Single low-weight report; he was killed anyway.

history.old: Consult the archive early, while the living population and your sample are largest; waiting risks dying with the token unused. Report the full sample, duplicates included. Never treat a role missing from the sample as absent from the game, or attach a sampled role to a particular player.
history.note: Moderator: Grace's 9 shown roles plus the flips of Frank, Mallory and Carol covered all 13 players and proved Heidi's Sheriff claim false. Alice, Heidi, Ivan, Olivia and Dave stressed sample-not-census, correct only until the gaps close.

history.old: Consult the archive early, while the living population and your sample are largest; waiting risks dying with the token unused. Report the full sample, duplicates included. A sample proves roles exist, not who holds them, and a missing role isn't absent. But count the gaps after every flip: once the unshown slots are all filled by flipped roles, the list plus flips is a full census, a role shown once has exactly one holder, and any counterclaim to it is a lie.
history.note: The old wording ('a sample proves roles exist', 'a full census once slots are filled') ignored the fakes in the list. In this game the listed Arsonist was real and was ignored.

entries.tip: Prioritize hanging the strongest killing-faction suspect over punishing a liar. An Executioner doesn't block a Village win, even when they behave hostilely. If you acquit one suspect to pursue a stronger one, first secure explicit Yes and Guilty votes for a same-day replacement, so the switch doesn't become another night of delay.

support.note: Grace, Olivia, Mallory and Ivan: after Frank claimed Executioner, the town switched to Heidi and hanged her the same day.
Moderator: the town wasted D6 hanging Frank, an Executioner whose Evil read was fully explained, while Heidi kept killing.
Moderator: on D4 Bob had effectively admitted Clerk, but the town spent the hang on Jester Grace's contested Medic claim instead.

entries.tip: If you will use intercepted PMs to prove a fake Eavesdropper claim, set up a consistent target early: the declared target must take part in the exchange on the following Day. Don't claim inactivity on nights you may later need, and don't retrofit a visit once visit totals constrain you. Quoting real PMs proves access, not Village alignment.

support.note: Moderator and Heidi: Heidi claimed inactivity on N1-N2, then at her D6 trial said she had eavesdropped on Niaj on N2. No vote changed, and she was hanged 4-2.

entries.tip: Argue comparative likelihood, not mere mechanical possibility. A legal alternative explanation is not evidence that it happened, and 'some other claim could be false' rarely beats several converging clues. Don't count several consequences of one disputed claim as independent confirmations. On defense, name the specific weak premise, explain why your account fits better, and offer a concrete test that tells them apart.

support.note: Carol, Ivan, Frank, Rupert, Niaj, Dave and Grace all made this point. Bob, Judy and Heidi's 'mechanically possible' defenses all failed.
Rupert's 'that claim is uncheckable, test it first' failed against a self-testing Oracle hit; Heidi's 'mechanically possible' second-Pharmacist defense failed too.
Alice and Bob: repeating 'unverified' changed no votes. Name the exact conditional link and ask the accused to disprove it, or offer a concrete alternative explanation.

entries.tip: (Village) An Evil Sheriff result on someone who claims Vanilla, a role that doesn't explain the result, is a real case, but it fits a Jester or Executioner (both read Evil, both have 0 tokens) as well as a Yakuza. 'Could be a frame' is a possibility, not evidence. Before the trial ask for a claim and an audit, and weigh whether the player has pushed for their own hang. If you hang, keep Guilty votes to a bare majority so a Jester's revenge has few targets. A claim that exactly explains the result but can't be checked (Ex-Con, Jester) is not an acquittal either. Plan a mechanical test that night: a Tracker or Lookout on the claimant (an Ex-Con visits someone every night), or an Oracle guess of 'Ex-Con'. Hang the next day if the test fails. A blocked or missing test is no result, not a clearance. If the Yakuza are near a voting majority, hang today instead of waiting.

support.note: Moderator: Olivia claimed Vanilla against Dave's N2 Evil result and was acquitted 0-12 on D3. She was the Ritualist who won the game on N6.

history.old: An Evil Sheriff result on someone who claims Vanilla, a role that doesn't explain the result, is a real case. 'Could be a frame or a Neutral' is a possibility, not evidence. Unless someone gives a specific counter-explanation, vote Guilty rather than acquit. Save extra caution for claims that actually explain the result (Ex-Con, Jester), and even then check the claim against the role's mechanics.
history.note: Moderator: Dave's real Evil on Carol was dismissed 0-10 after her uncheckable Ex-Con claim. Nobody pointed a Tracker at her, and Alice's Ex-Con guess was blocked. Carol was the Puppeteer and won.

history.note: Bob claimed Vanilla against Grace's N1 Evil, audited 0, and was hanged 13-0 as a Jester. The old wording ('vote Guilty') pushed the pile-on.

entries.tip: Learn the exact mechanics of the role you fake-claim before you first describe it, and get them right from the start. An Ex-Con visits a random player automatically every night, so never say 'I have no night action'. A claim that explains your Evil result is undone if your own words contradict the role text. Agree on the exact wording in night chat.

support.note: Moderator, Niaj, Carol, Alice and Bob: Niaj's Ex-Con claim fit his Evil result, but his repeated 'no night action' contradicted the automatic visit. He was hanged on D4 and flipped Clerk.

entries.tip: Don't leave the Katana for several nights on a member who also visits the victims with their own role (e.g. a Mortician cleaning the target). A cover action explains one visit, but the same sole visitor to every victim becomes a pattern Lookouts and Trackers chain together. Rotate the holder, or give it to a member with no action, once an info role is active.

Judy and Dave: with a Tracker alive, rotate the holder to a low-profile Grunt; Heidi's repeated visits were tracked.
Moderator: the visiting Diviner held the Katana all game and was caught by the Lookout.
Judy: a visible holder pattern made it easier for the town to read the Yakuza's moves.
Frank, Alice, moderator: Bob held the Katana N1-N5, and the map plus elimination made him the predictable holder at the D4 and D6 trials.

Moderator and Carol: Carol held the Katana and divined Grace on N2; Heidi's track showed Carol visiting Grace and Judy (the victim) and she was hanged 8-2. Grunt Bob then made five unexposed kills.

entries.tip: Hold your tokens until elimination makes an exact role near-certain. Late game, list the living players, the known Jester and the roles already seen, then name the last Neutral. A 2-token Divine guess kills through Standard Defense (Arsonist, SK) that stops the Katana, and it can win the game outright.

support.note: Moderator: Olivia saved both tokens through five nights. On N6 she deduced Heidi was the Arsonist, since Judy had openly played Jester and the ignite had happened. The Divine guess won the game.
Erin held both ritual tokens for four nights and never guessed, even with claimed Lookouts and a 'Medic' alive.

entries.tip: When you report X as the only other visitor to a victim, address your own omitted visit up front and present corroboration (a Tracker who saw you visit, earlier checked reports). Call it 'X visited', not 'X is proven the killer'. Overclaiming invites the self-visit caveat and can put you on trial.

support.note: Frank and the moderator: Frank overstated his true reports on Erin. The table fixated on the caveat, acquitted Erin and spent a trial on Frank.

Moderator, Carol, Dave, Mallory, Heidi, Ivan: Carol's five-name list was fully confirmed, but her '100% the killer is among these five' overclaim ignored her own visit. It gave Frank a counter-nomination and forced a third trial that ended D2.

entries.tip: Keep a self-declared Jester alive. The town won't hang them, so they soak up nominations and votes. At low counts they are a known non-Yakuza who blocks no win and helps you deduce the remaining Neutral by elimination.

support.note: Ivan: Judy self-nominated every day and was never hanged. At the final four she shielded the Yakuza and let Olivia identify Heidi as the Arsonist.

entries.tip: Weigh a visit report by when it was made. A watcher who names several visitors before any of them have spoken or claimed is very hard to fake. A list or counter-result that only repeats public claims is weak. Once such a list is trusted, make every named visitor explain their visit, then eliminate names as they flip or are confirmed until only the killer is left.

support.note: Heidi, Ivan, Niaj, Carol and Dave: Grace named Carol, Mallory and Niaj as Alice's visitors before they claimed. Dave's timeline check saved her on D2. By D4 Bob, Mallory and Frank had flipped and Niaj was confirmed, so only Carol (the SK) was left, and she was hanged.

entries.tip: Post your full visitor list early, before the visited players claim or explain their visits. When challenged, point out explicitly that you named them first; that timing is your strongest proof.

support.note: Moderator: Grace's N1 list on Alice (Bob, Carol, Frank, Mallory, Niaj) was the backbone of the Village win, and its timing saved her at trial.
Moderator: Carol's early list was confirmed by every named visitor and earned her near-confirmed status.

entries.tip: When two Sheriff claimants report the same result on a player who flips Good, the shared result confirms neither. The player may have been framed, and the fake may have framed them to match. Break the tie with an independent check on one claimant, and look at who visited the framed player that night.

support.note: Moderator: Bob and Frank both said Alice was Evil. Bob had framed her. Frank's N2 Evil check on Bob, plus Bob's Guilty vote on Grace, hanged Bob, who flipped Fabricator.

entries.tip: Expect a Neutral killer to hunt the same loud info roles you do. If the Katana keeps landing on the same player as another attack, it adds no kill. Spread the Katana to a second valuable target, and pair it with a block on the identified Medic.

support.note: Moderator: Mallory blocked Medic Niaj on N2 and N3, but Carol's SK attack hit the Katana's target both nights, so the Village kept its numbers.
Heidi's N3 Katana on Alice coincided with the SK's attack, so the double kill wasted the Yakuza night.

entries.tip: On a Day your Clerk has rigged, the rig executes any successful nominee whatever the verdict, so vote Innocent with the town on that trial, and don't let the Clerk be the nominator. A Guilty minority gets the rig announced, and that small Guilty bloc becomes the town's list of your team.

support.note: Grace was rig-hanged 3 Guilty to 12 Innocent. The only Guilty voters were Carol, Judy (the nominator) and Niaj, and the Village hanged exactly those three on D3-D5. Moderator, Carol and Judy reported this.
Bob and Ivan: all three Yakuza voted Guilty on the rigged Heidi trial. That vote bloc became a public record the town later used. On a rigged Day, split or vote Innocent.

entries.tip: Keep exact-role results separate from alignment. An Oracle WRONG rules out only the guessed role, not a faction, and a Roleplayer shows as 'Roleplayer' to exact-role checks. A RIGHT clears alignment only if the guessed role is a Village role. Use the miss to test the target's claim: it convicts when it disproves their claimed role and they then change their story.

support.note: Heidi, Ivan, Mallory, Rupert, Judy and Bob: Dave's wrong guess 'Bob = Pharmacist' was correctly not read as Evil, and Bob (Cardinal) was spared. His wrong guess 'Erin = Vanilla' disproved Erin's claim, and her pivots then convicted her.
Judy: a correct guess confirms the role only. Her Jester RIGHT on Carol voided Carol's fake Sheriff result.

entries.tip: Eavesdrop on whoever starts the Day 1 PM cluster. When you intercept incriminating private messages, post them publicly in full and write the exact quotes and every implicated player into your will before your turn ends. Expect a Ritualist or the Katana that night, so your will must carry the case without you.

support.note: Alice targeted Carol after her D1 PM cluster and read Carol's Katana plan to Judy and Niaj live. Niaj's Divine guess killed Alice that night, but her published quotes and will hanged all three Yakuza. Alice and the moderator reported this.

entries.tip: A hard-claimed investigator is a sure guess, and a 2-token Divine guess goes through any Medic. But the kill only helps if it lands before they publish: once their evidence is public and in their will, killing them saves nothing. Don't spend guesses on claims contested by a dead Oracle; prefer claims verified by an independent source.

support.note: Niaj's Divine 'Alice = Eavesdropper' killed her through Olivia's Standard protection, but she had already posted Carol's PMs and written them into her will. Moderator and Niaj reported this.
Heidi, Mallory and Dave: Heidi's correct Standard guess on claimed Lookout Carol failed to the Medic's Standard Defense on N2. Use Divine on likely-protected claimants.
Moderator, Peggy: the Divine guess 'Heidi = Surveyor' killed her through Mallory's Standard protection without outing Peggy.

entries.tip: Never reuse a teammate's failed fake claim. Once a claim has been exposed and the claimant flipped Yakuza, the same claim from you is read as a team script.

support.note: Judy claimed Jester after Carol's Jester claim had been disproven by a visit and Carol flipped Puppeteer. The town dismissed it at once. Judy's reflection.

entries.tip: Post your automatic random pair every night in your first speech, with the night and 'random' or 'chosen', even when it seems useless. A Seer's pair is guaranteed, so a missing one looks like a fake claim and gives opponents a ready attack line. If you forgot one, say so plainly and post it at once. Put every result in your will the same Day.

support.note: Moderator, Heidi, Mallory, Judy: Heidi never posted her N2 pair. Alice built her defense and will on the gap, and Ivan, Carol and Dave pressed it on D4 before Heidi posted it.

entries.tip: Know which claimed results are automatic (a Seer's nightly pair) and which need tokens or actions. Ask promptly about an unreported automatic result: it is a concrete, testable question. But treat the gap as something to be explained, not proof of a lie, and remember random pairs can repeat.

support.note: Erin, Ivan, Frank, Heidi, Dave: Heidi's missing N2 pair was pressed, and she was saved once she posted it. Frank and Heidi noted that repeated pairs are legal.

entries.tip: Agree on one cover story for the whole team in night chat. Never publicly or privately assign a teammate's claimed role to another player, e.g. calling someone else 'the Vigilante' after your teammate claimed it. The contradiction exposes both of you.

support.note: Moderator: Carol claimed Vigilante while Dave argued in public and by PM to Erin that Ivan was the Vigilante. Erin and Heidi used it to hang Dave, and Ivan shot Carol.

entries.tip: Don't send extra Yakuza visitors to the Katana target. A redundant block on an unprotected victim adds a second Yakuza name to any Lookout's list on that target. Before anyone fake-claims an investigator or Vanilla, check that the team's real visits that night can't contradict it.

support.note: Moderator: on N1 Olivia blocked Alice while Mallory killed her. Bob's Lookout list (Mallory, Olivia) broke Mallory's Sheriff claim and Olivia's Vanilla claim, and both were hanged.
Frank and Dave both visited Olivia on N1 (Katana plus clean); Mallory's watch named both and slot math finished them.

entries.tip: If a Sheriff reads you Evil, give one consistent claim early and name your target immediately. An unclaimed Evil-read player becomes everyone's fallback hang, and a target withheld until a second nomination looks invented.

support.note: Moderator, Frank, Judy and Olivia: Frank refused to claim from D2 to D6, named Judy as his target only late, and was hanged on D6 as the 'last Yakuza'.

entries.tip: Get the reason for a kill or a missing kill right before arguing from it. A role-block on the victim doesn't stop the attack on them; only blocking the Katana holder does. A kill can also fail to protection or innate Defense. List every explanation before building a case or a cover story on one.

support.note: Niaj wrongly argued that Olivia's block on Alice cancelled the Katana, which hurt his credibility. Olivia, Ivan and Heidi warned against overconfident causal stories.

entries.tip: A Philanthropist's gift notice tells the recipient only that some Philanthropist acted, not who. A claimed recipient's 'confirmation' doesn't verify a particular Philanthropist claimant, and a token count or will written before the gift may be out of date.

support.note: Dave, Mallory and Olivia all stressed reading gift feedback literally.
Erin: track gifts as submitted actions, and record separately what the recipient's later account or will actually confirms.

entries.tip: Never send a Village player a private request you couldn't defend if they posted it (e.g. 'block the Medic tonight'). Unknown players publish such requests, and they become the town's clearest evidence against you.

support.note: Moderator: Carol asked Frank (Party Animal) by PM to block Niaj. Frank posted it, and Olivia and Peggy called it the clearest act of the day.

entries.tip: Cross group results (Surveyor, Diviner, census-type alignment counts) with token audits, flips and independently corroborated claims to eliminate candidates. A nonzero token count rules out tokenless roles (Arsonist, Serial Killer, Jester, Grunt, Vanilla), and a flip removes that player. A 'k of 3 Good' count becomes a named suspect once the other members are confirmed: nominate and vote on it rather than waiting for a direct contradiction. Remember that an alignment count reads true alignment, so a non-Good slot may be a Neutral, not a Yakuza. A player's own claim is a claim, not corroboration. State which reports the elimination depends on, then press the last candidate. A Vanilla claim doesn't explain a survey slot.

support.note: Moderator, Frank, Ivan and Judy: Judy's survey said one of Ivan/Mallory/Niaj was the Arsonist. Alice's audit showed Niaj with 1 token, and Mallory flipped Mortician. That isolated Ivan, who was hanged.
Moderator, Carol, Ivan: Carol's N1 count of one Evil among Bob, Dave and Heidi, plus Dave's and Heidi's Good flips, isolated Bob, who was hanged D4.
Heidi: remove known-Good players from census groups, remember Neutrals aren't counted as Good, and chain groups across nights; her census put Judy in the bad group.

A nonzero token count rules out tokenless roles (Arsonist, Serial Killer, Jester, Grunt, Vanilla), and a flip removes that player. State which reports the elimination depends on, then press the last candidate. A Vanilla claim doesn't explain a survey slot.
history.note: Moderator, Heidi, Bob, Erin: Heidi's census plus Alice's flip and Dave's Eavesdropper claim (backed by Carol's survey) isolated Frank, who flipped Clerk. Bob and Erin initially treated the census as naming nobody.

entries.tip: Don't play clean. Voting with confirmed town and claiming Vanilla gives you no route to a hanging, and a town with confirmed power roles will hang real Evil instead of you. Build suspicion by midgame with odd votes, a shaky but committed claim or an aggressive push, so you look plausibly Yakuza. Don't confess a fake claim and then self-nominate again and again: that marks you as a Jester, and the table refuses your trials for days. If you reach a small endgame where your vote decides a trial between a killer and the Village, trade your vote for a promised Guilty on your next self-nomination.

Moderator, Dave, Judy: Judy self-nominated about 15 times and PM'd five players for Guilty votes. Mallory called it a Jester pattern on D2, and every trial ended Innocent.

history.old: Don't play clean. Voting with confirmed town and claiming Vanilla gives you no route to a hanging, and a town with confirmed power roles will hang real Evil instead of you. Build suspicion by midgame with odd votes, a shaky but committed claim or an aggressive push.
history.note: Moderator: Frank's confessed fake Sheriff claim and 7+ self-nominations were refused (trials 4-6 and 1-9, later only 1-3 Yes votes). He won only because the D7 final three made his vote decisive and Bob promised him a hang. Frank's own lesson says to self-nominate sparingly.

entries.tip: Before accepting a chain of claims that corroborate each other, list which links are independently verified. Verified links include a flip, a token audit, a tracked visit, an Oracle check, a survived attack that matches a Medic's claimed protection, and a block notice confirmed by its target. A chain with no verified link is a story, not evidence. Name which single link could be tested tonight and what would still follow if it were false. Don't swing to ignoring the map, though. If its links hold up and it leaves one living candidate, that candidate stays the top case. Don't acquit them and then spend the hang on someone whose checkable record is clean but whose nominations misfired. If you won't hang the candidate today, block or track them that night.

support.note: Olivia, Judy, Grace and Erin: Niaj's claimed Strong protection on Erin went untested, and the Erin/Niaj chain stood on one unverified claim for four days.
Carol: the D3 hang of Vanilla Carol rested on a chain of a survey pool plus an unverified Sheriff claim. Test one link directly first.

history.old: Before accepting a chain of claims that corroborate each other, list which links are independently verified (a flip, a token audit, a tracked visit, an Oracle check). A chain with no verified link is a story, not evidence. Name which single link could be tested tonight and what would still follow if it were false.

entries.tip: (Cardinal) Stay hidden while safe. Your curse hits only Good players, so to the Yakuza you are a two-for-one kill. Claim Vanilla publicly if pressed, but put the true Cardinal claim in your will so the town reads the random Good death correctly. If a Vigilante may shoot you or the Village is about to hang you, claim Cardinal at once. Once an archive or survey exposes you anyway, ask openly for protection, because the Yakuza now want you dead.

Claim Vanilla publicly if pressed, but put the true Cardinal claim in your will so the town reads the random Good death correctly if you die. If a Vigilante may shoot you or the Village is about to hang you, claim Cardinal at once, since your death Divine-attacks a random Good player.

entries.tip: When a player reveals night knowledge they shouldn't have (e.g. that someone was role-blocked before anyone posted it), only a blocker or a Yakuza could know it. Ask for the source at once, before they settle on a story. Then switch the day's hang to them: vote Innocent on the current trial and nominate the slipper. Don't let an older, weaker case keep your Guilty vote, and make your vote match what you just said. A blocker claim made afterwards to explain the slip must still fit the Tracker and Lookout logs.

support.note: Moderator, Erin, Frank, Niaj: on D3 Heidi named Alice's private N2 block. Alice and Niaj caught it, but Bob, who had said he wouldn't hang Erin, cast the deciding Guilty on Erin (SK). The town held 5 of 9 votes and could have hanged Heidi.

entries.tip: When a Sheriff catches a teammate, counterclaim the one role that fully explains the result (Ex-Con for an Evil read) and describe its mechanics exactly. That night, have the Pharmacist block the player most likely to test the claim (an Oracle, Tracker or Lookout), kill the Sheriff, and have the Mortician clean them so the role and will stay hidden.

entries.tip: When the town is set to hang a rival Neutral killer, add your Guilty votes. It removes a threat to you, keeps your record clean, and uses up the town's hang on a non-Yakuza.

support.note: Moderator: all four Yakuza voted Guilty on Erin (SK), securing the 5-of-9 hang on the day the town should have hanged Heidi.

entries.tip: A correct accusation or a Guilty vote against a Neutral killer doesn't certify the accuser. Yakuza gain from removing a rival killer and from the credibility it buys. Judge each later push on its own evidence.

support.note: Grace: the Yakuza voted with the town on Erin (SK), then used the same bloc to hang Vanilla Bob and Frank.

entries.tip: A Veteran on alert Strong-attacks every non-Astral visitor. If a claimed Veteran says they alerted on a night when a living player visited them, the claim is false. Investigators who visited a claimed Veteran should say so publicly as a direct test of the alert story.

support.note: Ivan audited Erin on N4 and survived, while Erin said she alerted that night; with the 0-token audit this hanged the Serial Killer D5. Bob, Erin, Ivan and the moderator reported this.

entries.tip: Never visit a claimed, contested or likely Veteran at night: no protections, no watches, no audits. A Veteran's alert Strong-attacks every visitor whatever their faction. The Yakuza visit by choice and simply stay away, so the only players a known Veteran kills are your own Medic and investigators. A Veteran on alert already has Standard Defense, so protecting them gains nothing. Above all, never visit on a night the Veteran said they would alert. To verify a Veteran, use visit-free or Astral checks, or wait for their alert reports. If a Veteran hasn't claimed, ask them to claim first, or coordinate so that at most one investigator takes the risk.

support.note: Moderator: after Erin's fake Veteran claim, Alice tracked and Niaj checked the silent Olivia on N4. Olivia was on alert and killed both confirmed power roles.

history.old: When a Veteran claim is contested, or a likely Veteran hasn't claimed, don't visit that player at night. Ask them to claim first or coordinate so at most one investigator takes the risk. A real Veteran's alert kills your own investigators.
history.note: Moderator (0.4), Grace (0.16): claimed Veteran Dave's alerts killed only Medic Alice (protecting him N2) and Lookout Judy (watching him N4). The Yakuza night chat said 'nobody visits Dave' every night.
