A Veteran's alert Strong-attacks every visitor whatever their faction, and the Yakuza, who visit by choice, simply stay away, so the only players a known Veteran kills are your own Medic and investigators. If a Veteran hasn't claimed, ask them to claim first or coordinate so at most one investigator takes the risk.
history.note: Moderator (0.4): Dave announced his N2 alert and Accountant Frank audited him that night and died. On N3 Medic Alice protected the alerting Dave and also died, with both tokens unspent. That was two self-inflicted Village deaths.

entries.tip: If someone claims Veteran while you are unclaimed, counterclaim that Day, or at least signal clearly that the claim is false. Silence makes you the obvious unclaimed target for town investigators, and your alert will kill your own side.

support.note: Moderator: Olivia stayed silent after Erin's D4 fake Veteran claim, alerted N4 and killed Tracker Alice and Sheriff Niaj, leaving a 1-in-4 endgame.

entries.tip: As a solo killer (0 tokens), don't fake-claim a token role like Veteran while an Accountant may be alive, and don't claim alerts on nights someone may have visited you. Check any public role list and the living claims first. Prefer a tokenless, no-visit-sensitive claim you can hold.

support.note: Erin (SK) claimed Veteran with 'conserved alerts'. Ivan's audit showed 0 tokens and he had visited her on her claimed alert night, so she was hanged D5. Moderator and Erin reported this.

entries.tip: On Night 1 several investigators may land on the same player. Consider skipping the kill, or give the Katana to a member whose claim will match the visit, the token count and a Not Evil read. The holder's Not Evil result is a known tell, not a cover.

support.note: Moderator: Carol dropped a no-kill plan and attacked Mallory on N1. She was tracked, audited (2 tokens) and read Not Evil the same night, and was hanged D2.

entries.tip: Post an audit result as its own message before any nomination, with the expected count for the claimed role. Bundling the audit with a nomination makes the trial look like a setup and lets the accused argue about timing instead of the numbers.

support.note: Judy and Carol: Ivan posted his audit of Carol in the same message as his nomination, and Carol used the timing to call it a convenient counterclaim.

entries.tip: Spend your chosen-pair token on the first night the pair matters, and post the result that Day. A claimed investigator is a likely night-kill target, and a held token dies with you.

support.note: Judy held her token for N2 and was killed that night before she could share the result.
Judy claimed Seer on D2 with her token unspent and was killed N2, so the token died with her.
Moderator: Judy kept her chosen-pair token 'for a stronger night' and died with it.
Judy: she spent her chosen pair late (Carol/Heidi SAME) and died before anyone could use it; spend it early when it can be cross-checked.

entries.tip: If one player is killed by two different attacks in one night (e.g. Serial Killer and Katana), there are two independent killers alive. Keep both in the suspect pool and don't assume one killer explains every death.

support.note: Judy: Bob died to both the Serial Killer and the Katana on the same night, and Erin (SK) kept killing after the Yakuza fell.
Frank: on N5 the ignite, the Katana and the Cardinal curse all fired together. Check every death's cause before assuming a single killer.
Heidi: Frank died on N4 to both the ignite and the Katana, and the revealed causes showed two killers.
Frank, Grace, Ivan, Judy: the N4 multi-death with no Katana explanation pointed to an Arsonist ignite.

entries.tip: Never be part of a small Guilty minority on a Village claimant whose results the table has already confirmed (e.g. a Lookout whose named visitors all confirmed their visits). The few Guilty votes mark exactly who wanted them dead, and every later trial cites them.

support.note: Moderator and Carol: Heidi and Mallory were the only Guilty votes on Carol after all five visitors she named had confirmed. Carol called it out on the spot, and the town cited it in later trials.

Moderator: Bob, Frank and Judy were the only Guilty votes on both of the D4 trials (Carol and Heidi, each 3-6). The town asked them to justify it at once, and Bob was nominated within minutes. This game had public votes.

Moderator: on D2 the only Guilty votes on Oracle Mallory were Bob, Carol and Ivan, the whole Yakuza team, and the trial failed 3-7. After Carol flipped, Alice and Erin pressed Bob and Ivan over that vote daily, which led to both prosecutions. This game had public ballots, but under secret ballots a small Guilty total still gets compared with stated votes.

entries.tip: If you survive a night attack while claimed, say so publicly that Day: a Ritualist whose guess was right will try again. Medic: stay on a claimant who was the target of an exact-role attack, because the Ritualist already knows the guess was right.

support.note: Moderator: on N2 Heidi's Standard Ritualist guess on Lookout Carol was stopped by Bob's protection. Carol mentioned it only in her will, Bob moved to Ivan on N3, and Heidi's last token killed Carol.

entries.tip: (Everyone) A night with no Katana kill right after a blocker hit player X is a lead that X holds the Katana, strongest when only one Yakuza can be left (Sheriff checks then read the holder Not Evil anyway). Verify the blocker first: a blocked player confirming the block publicly, or the only other blocker role (Pharmacist) already flipped. A lone holder can skip a night on purpose to frame the block target, and a kill can also fail to protection, so one match is weak. Two or more matches with a confirmed blocker log is a real mechanical case to hang on.

support.note: Ivan blocked Mallory N2 and Heidi N4, both no-kill nights; Olivia confirmed her N3 block after Pharmacist Niaj had flipped. Heidi was hanged D5 as the last Yakuza. Reported by Ivan, Dave, Erin, Grace, Judy, Carol, Frank, Olivia and the moderator; Alice added the skip-to-frame caveat.

entries.tip: (Yakuza) Once a Party Animal or other Village blocker claims and posts a block log, kill them next with the Katana. Every block that lands on the holder makes a block/no-kill match the town treats as proof, and a lone last holder can't afford even one. Don't spend the Katana on other targets while the blocker lives.

support.note: Ivan claimed D3 after stopping Mallory's N2 kill. Heidi attacked Alice (already the SK's target) and Erin instead; Ivan's N4 block on her produced a no-kill night and she was hanged. Mallory, Niaj, Heidi and the moderator reported this.
Moderator, Peggy: Niaj blocked the holder on N3-N5 and publicly claimed it from D4. The Yakuza never targeted him and lost three kills.
Moderator: the Yakuza left Party Animal Grace alive. Her N4 block on holder Frank cost a kill, and her N5 death came only after she stopped blocking him.

entries.tip: (Village) An exact-role hit (Oracle RIGHT) on an unverifiable claimant tests itself on the flip: a fake hit would hang its own claimant the next day. A last Yakuza can't even know who the hidden Neutral is. Hang the named player at once; 'test the claimant first' only buys the killer another night. Claimants should say this explicitly when posting.

support.note: Erin's RIGHT 'Rupert = Serial Killer' hanged the SK on D4. Carol, Frank, Erin and Rupert (whose 'test it first' defense failed) reported this.

entries.tip: Guess the role the evidence points to. If a player is openly begging to be hanged or keeps self-nominating, guess 'Jester' on them early. Post the RIGHT before any nomination of them can pass: it shuts down the Jester's (and an Executioner's) win and frees the Day's trials for Yakuza. Don't re-guess a player whose role is already settled. Without a list, don't guess 'Grunt' blind, since it is often absent. Once a public role list (archive, survey) shows Yakuza roles, guess the roles still unaccounted for against the top suspects; a listed Grunt narrowed by slot math is a good guess. Also try Serial Killer behind an early, unprompted Vanilla claim once Neutral kills appear. Or try a common action Yakuza role (Pharmacist, Diviner, Clerk) on a suspected Yakuza. One RIGHT on a killer ends the debate. Stay unclaimed until you hold a RIGHT result that changes a vote.

support.note: Erin wasted N1-N2 guessing Grunt (Bob was Jester, Mallory Clerk); her N3 'Serial Killer' on Rupert was right. Erin, Grace and the moderator.

against.note: Moderator: the 'never spend a guess on a likely Jester' clause was wrong here. Carol's N1 Jester guess on the self-nominating Judy shut down every Jester hang and let the Village hunt Yakuza.

history.old: (Oracle) Don't spend guesses on 'Grunt'; it is often absent. Guess the role the evidence points to: Serial Killer behind an early, unprompted Vanilla claim once Neutral kills appear, or a common action Yakuza role (Pharmacist, Diviner, Clerk) on a suspected Yakuza. One RIGHT on a killer ends the debate. Stay unclaimed until you hold a RIGHT result.
history.note: Moderator: with Pharmacist and Grunt unaccounted for among Bob, Frank and Ivan, Mallory guessed 'Frank = Pharmacist' on N4 and N5, though Frank was an obvious Jester. 'Bob = Grunt' or 'Ivan = Pharmacist' would have been right.

history.old: Guess the role the evidence points to. Without a list, don't guess 'Grunt' blind, since it is often absent. Once a public role list (archive, survey) shows Yakuza roles, guess the roles still unaccounted for against the top suspects; a listed Grunt narrowed by slot math is a good guess. Also try Serial Killer behind an early, unprompted Vanilla claim once Neutral kills appear, or a common action Yakuza role (Pharmacist, Diviner, Clerk) on a suspected Yakuza. Never spend a guess on a player whose behaviour already marks them as a likely Jester (a confessed fake claim, repeated self-nominations). One RIGHT on a killer ends the debate. Stay unclaimed until you hold a RIGHT result.
history.note: Moderator: Carol's N1 'Judy = Jester' guess, claimed D2, stopped all six Jester/Executioner hangs, and her later right guesses (Dave Executioner, Bob Lookout) made her credible. The old 'never guess a likely Jester' clause would have forbidden the game's most valuable check.

entries.tip: (Serial Killer) Don't kill Yakuza early: each one you remove strengthens a large town against you. Hit Village power roles (blockers, Sheriff, Accountant) and turn on the Yakuza only when the town is small. Don't attack the player the Yakuza obviously want dead (e.g. a Lookout who just exposed their holder); a double kill wastes your night and shows you are still active. Don't volunteer a Vanilla claim early when nobody pressed you; it is the first claim exact-role checkers test once SK kills appear.

support.note: Rupert killed Pharmacist Niaj N1 and Clerk Mallory N2, hit Alice alongside the Katana N3, volunteered Vanilla on D2, and was Oracle-hit and hanged D4. Rupert and the moderator.

entries.tip: (Trapper) A publicly announced trap on a confirmed investigator deters killers, who will route around that player, so it works like protection. But a lone holder simply avoids the predictable target, so a hidden trap is the one that actually catches someone: choose between deterrence and catching. Traps arm only from the next night, so aim at whoever the Katana is likely to hit in two nights. A silent trap also gives free negative info: report it as 'no non-Village visitor to X'. If a Lookout reveals your visit to a victim, claim at once with mechanics others can check.

support.note: Judy announced a trap on Sheriff Grace; Rupert never attacked Grace, and Grace survived. Judy noted a lone holder avoids a claimed Sheriff's trap. Her immediate Trapper claim cleared her Lookout sighting. Conflicts partly with t86.

entries.tip: (Village) Once several Yakuza have flipped, the last one usually hides behind a late, uncheckable Vanilla claim from a player who stayed unclaimed and echoed others while asking investigators to claim. Do slot math on the flipped Yakuza roles, and test those claims first with blocks, exact-role guesses and audits. A Not Evil read on them means nothing, since the lone Yakuza holds the Katana.

support.note: Heidi (Diviner) claimed Vanilla late and was hanged D5 as the last Yakuza. Erin, Ivan, Judy, Olivia and Carol.

entries.tip: (Yakuza) Don't give several teammates the same fake Vanilla claim or will. Once one flips with a fake Vanilla will, every later Vanilla claim looks scripted. Vary covers, and give each member a token-consistent claim with a night action that explains possible visits, set before Day 3. A Vanilla claim made only when pressed late is exactly where the town looks.

support.note: Several Yakuza wrote fake Vanilla wills; Heidi's late Vanilla claim was hanged. Carol, Erin, Niaj, Heidi, Mallory and Peggy.
Moderator: both Yakuza took the same Vanilla cover, which drew suspicion to both once the archive was public.

entries.tip: (Jester) Make yourself the town's concrete lead. A mild but reasonable Day 1 dissent (e.g. 'a no-hang day gives Yakuza a free night') draws N1 checks, and you read Evil to the Sheriff. One short Day 1 PM to a single pushy or quiet player becomes a link if they flip Yakuza. On trial, claim Vanilla (it matches your 0 tokens), give a short, weak defense that blames the accuser, and vote Guilty on yourself. A strong defense or any Jester hint makes careful players vote Innocent.

support.note: Bob did exactly this; Grace's Evil check plus his PM to Pharmacist Niaj got him hanged 13-0 for the win.
Moderator, Carol: Carol's D1 surrender and self-Guilty votes read as Jester bait. Judy's N3 Jester guess was right, and the town refused every Carol trial after that.
Grace: she voted Guilty on herself, which counts toward the majority, and gave a plausible but weak defense. She was hanged 4-0. Under secret ballots the self-vote is also hidden.
Grace: voting Guilty on herself added to the majority, and a plausible but breakable claim got her hanged.

entries.tip: (Accountant) Audit claimed tokenless visitors and quiet unclaimed players. When posting, state which roles the count rules in and out rather than only the raw number: a raw 3 can out a hidden Vigilante. A 0 rules out Medic, Vigilante, Veteran and Prosecutor but fits Jester, Executioner, SK and Vanilla, so say so; a 3 fits no Yakuza starting role. Remember a Jester also audits 0.

support.note: Carol's 0 on Bob fit a Jester but nobody weighed it; she kept Olivia's count vague and Olivia stayed hidden. Carol, Bob and Niaj.

entries.tip: (Diviner) Picking yourself gives you Strong Defense for the night but no reading; do it once you hold the Katana and expect a block or attack. Early on, use draws to find Neutrals as well as power roles, and report every draw to the team in night chat before the Day's votes. A Jester drawn in a group whose member later reads Evil (and isn't your teammate) is almost surely that player: then vote Innocent on him and never block or target him.

support.note: Heidi's N1 divine on Bob/Carol/Dave drew Jester, but the team still voted Guilty on Bob and lost Peggy to the revenge. Heidi, Dave, Niaj, Mallory, Peggy and the moderator.

entries.tip: (Puppeteer) Your puppet lapses if you die the night you spend it (R21), so don't spend the token on a night with elevated death risk, such as after voting Guilty on a likely Jester. Use it early, while it can still swing a trial, rather than hoarding it until the team is thin.

support.note: Peggy puppeted Judy for D3 but died to Jester revenge that night, so the token was wasted.
Moderator and Frank: Grace died on D4 still holding her puppet token and never puppeted Dave or Bob on D3-D4, the Days that decided the game.
Ivan held his puppet until N5, spent it, and died to the ignite that night, so it lapsed.
Ivan and the moderator: the puppet was held N1-N5, spent the night Ivan died, and lapsed. Use it while teammates are alive.
Moderator: Bob never used his puppet and was hanged on D4 still holding it.
Moderator: Heidi never used her puppet token and was hanged D4 still holding it.

entries.tip: (Medic) If you were visible on Day 1, consider spending 1 token on Night 1 for Standard self-protection. Night 1 Katana targets are usually the most visible talkers, and a Medic dead on N1 saves nobody all game.

support.note: Dave's reflection: he organized D1 and was killed N1 with tokens unused.

entries.tip: (Everyone) When asking the town to hang on your single unverifiable log or result, commit publicly: 'if they flip Village, hang me next.' It costs an honest claimant little and makes the town willing to act today.

support.note: Ivan's reflection on the D5 Heidi hang on his block log.

entries.tip: Never claim a role that exists only on the Yakuza side (Mortician, Clerk, Diviner, Puppeteer, Ballot Stuffer, Wiretap, Pharmacist, etc.), whether as a fake claim or as the truth. That includes a role-limited hedge like 'my Puppeteer role took no action', which names your role as clearly as a claim. Any Good player can point out that a Village player can't hold it, and one Sheriff check finishes you. Before Day 2, agree in night chat on a safe Village claim for each member. It must fit the unseen archive slots and your token count, and it must hold up when a neighbour-based survey or slot math corners you. When asked about your night actions, answer with that prepared claim in one plain sentence.

support.note: Moderator, Carol and Heidi: Frank's survey cornered Carol, she claimed Mortician, Olivia noted no Good player can be Mortician, Dave's Evil check hanged her 6-2 on D4.
Ivan publicly claimed Puppeteer on D5. Erin pointed out at once that it was a Yakuza role from the archive; only the ignite stopped his hanging. Reported by the moderator and Erin.

Moderator: Bob, asked about his N1-3 actions, said 'my Puppeteer role took no action'. Carol pointed out it is a Yakuza role, and he was hanged 6-3 that Day.
Moderator: Carol hinted at an unposted N1 result for two days, then claimed Diviner. Erin, Grace and Mallory pointed out at once that it is a Yakuza role.
Moderator, Dave, Erin: Carol said 'I'm Good' on D2, then claimed Diviner (a Yakuza role) on D3; the table pointed it out at once and she was hanged 8-2.
Frank and Mallory: after the audits broke their Vanilla claims, Mallory switched to Clerk and Carol to Smuggler, both Yakuza-only roles, under nomination. Both were hanged 7-2 and 7-1.

entries.tip: A Cardinal's curse Divine-attacks a random living Good player, so killing a Cardinal costs the Village two players. Don't avoid a confirmed Cardinal as 'dangerous'. Read death-trigger roles to see which side they actually punish, and count the curse as a second kill when you choose a Katana target.

support.note: Moderator, Bob, Carol, Frank, Erin, Heidi: the Yakuza avoided Alice on N2. Grace corrected this, Alice was killed N3, and the curse killed Archivist Erin.

entries.tip: An Executioner or Jester pushing a target doesn't make the target innocent. If the target has their own hard contradiction (e.g. an Evil Sheriff result against a Vanilla claim, from a Sheriff who survived a Katana), hang on that evidence. The Executioner's win doesn't block yours. Limit the cost: keep Guilty votes near a bare majority so the revenge has a small pool, and keep confirmed power roles off the Guilty side.

support.note: Bob (Clerk) was hanged 12-1 on Dave's Evil result while Heidi (Executioner) pushed. Heidi won, and the revenge hit Yakuza Grace. Alice, Dave and Frank felt 'who benefits' should have stopped it, but the hang was correct for the Village.

entries.tip: Pressure your target on Day 1 so they make a weak or bare claim (e.g. Vanilla). Then attach yourself to the first hard result against them, keep repeating that result rather than your own opinion, and stay calm when your PMs are questioned. Argue in public; private Yes-vote requests become the case against you.

support.note: Moderator and Heidi: Heidi's D1 pressure pushed Bob into Vanilla. She hammered Dave's Evil result and won on D3, though her PMs drew suspicion. Partly conflicts with t104's 'stay quiet'.

Moderator: Dave opened with a friendly PM to Judy, let her self-nominate and steer, built the case on her own plays, and nominated her when the room was irritated. The nomination passed 10-1 and he won.

entries.tip: Once an ignite kills several players, the Arsonist must have made one douse visit per victim on earlier nights. The prime suspect is a living Vanilla or no-action claimant whom nobody watched, not a player whose visits to the victims are already explained (an Eavesdropper's or a Medic's). Once Neutral killers are possible, point a Lookout or Tracker at unverified Vanilla claimants early. When using douse math to clear someone, account for every night: one observed visit elsewhere rules out only that night's douse, not the others.

support.note: Moderator, Bob, Niaj, Olivia, Alice, Erin: Rupert claimed Vanilla, was never watched N1-N5, doused four and ignited. On D6 the town hanged Eavesdropper Grace for visiting victims, after Olivia 'cleared' Mallory from a single N2 visit.

entries.tip: In an endgame of three with a Jester alive (a killer, which may be the last Yakuza or a solo Neutral, plus a Villager and the Jester), the Jester's vote decides every trial. Hanging the Jester gives him his win and removes no killer, and the killer then kills the last Villager that night. Village: never vote Guilty on the Jester there. Make the killer's hang the only goal and win the Jester's vote by negotiating, not with ultimatums. Pass his self-nominations early (a Yes only starts the trial), so the killer must vote publicly on any hang he promised, and expose a broken promise while you still have votes. If the numbers allow hanging the Jester without leaving you alone with the killer, that is also an option, because his win doesn't block yours. Killer: you can buy the Jester's Innocent by promising a Guilty on his next self-nomination, but weigh the revenge draw on Guilty voters.

support.note: Moderator, Niaj, Olivia, Mallory: Olivia and Mallory voted No on every Carol self-nomination D8-D9. Rupert's promise went untested until D10, when he voted Innocent three times, and he then ignited the rest.
Moderator: Ivan's D7 hang left Bob (last Yakuza), Grace and Jester Frank; Frank would never vote Guilty on Bob, so Grace was doomed.

history.old: In an endgame with a known Jester and a lone solo killer, hanging the killer ends the game at once and the Jester loses. So the Jester will side with the killer unless given another route. The killer will promise to hang the Jester but can't afford the revenge draw. Pass the Jester's self-nominations early (a Yes only starts the trial), so the killer must vote publicly on the hang he promised, and expose the broken promise while you still have votes. Negotiate rather than issue ultimatums. If the numbers allow, hanging the Jester is also an option, because the Jester's win doesn't block yours.
history.note: Moderator: on D7 at Bob/Erin/Frank, Bob privately promised Frank a Guilty on his next self-nomination. Frank voted Innocent on Bob, Erin then voted Guilty on Frank and gave the Jester his win, and Bob killed Erin that night. Bob, Erin, Grace and Heidi gave similar lessons.

entries.tip: As a solo killer, claim Vanilla early and vote with legitimate town wagons on real Yakuza to build a clean ledger. Never douse or visit a player an investigator is likely watching. Redirect suspicion onto players with visible visits to the victims. In a small endgame with a known Jester, recruit them with the true fact that your hanging ends the game with them alive, so they lose, and promise to help hang them later.

support.note: Moderator and Rupert: Rupert pushed Grace's visits to get her hanged on D6. He then kept Carol voting No/Innocent on him for three Days with the R1 argument and won.

entries.tip: Before each endgame trial, work out each consequence separately. Who is left after the death? Does the R1 check end the game (Jesters and Executioners are ignored)? Is a Jester or Executioner win earned? A hang wins for them however the game ends. Can revenge still happen? It needs a following night and a living Guilty voter. Never accept an opponent's version of these rules.

support.note: Bob, Carol, Dave, Heidi, Judy, Olivia, Erin, Mallory, Frank: several players argued the R1 and Jester-win interaction wrongly in the D8-D10 endgame.
Dave and Mallory: with two players alive, a nomination needs both Yes votes. Dave couldn't force Mallory onto trial, and she ignited him.
Carol, Dave, Alice: with two alive a nomination needs both votes, so Carol could never force Mallory onto trial and was ignited.
Heidi and Mallory: at two alive a nomination needs both Yes votes, so Mallory could never hang Arsonist Heidi and was ignited.

entries.tip: (Village) Test every claimed investigation or protection by its visit footprint. A Sheriff check, chosen Seer pair, track or protection visits its target. A Lookout watching that target should list the claimant. A Scout or Cartographer group result must also put the claimant and target in the same group that night, so a credible Scout report naming them as members of different groups breaks the claim. Compare every claimed visit against every watch, track and group log before voting. A missing visit that a corroborated log should have shown breaks the claimed action. Then consider a Roleplayer or a Jester before reading it as faction.

support.note: Dave, Erin, Ivan and the moderator: Erin's watch on Ivan, corroborated by Alice's track, showed no visit from Mallory, which broke her Sheriff claim. She flipped Yakuza.
Moderator, Carol, Judy, Mallory: Alice's Scout result put Ivan and his claimed N3 track target Frank in different groups, which broke the Tracker claim. He flipped Yakuza.
Alice and Frank: Alice's Lookout list on Dave showed no visit from claimed Sheriff Grace, which broke the claim. Grace turned out to be the Jester, so run the Jester check too.

history.old: Test every claimed investigation by its visit footprint. A Sheriff check, chosen Seer pair, track or protection visits its target, so a Lookout watching that target should list the claimant. Compare every claimed visit against every watch and track log before voting. A missing visit that a corroborated log should have shown breaks the claimed action. Then consider Roleplayer before reading it as faction.
history.note: Alice, Frank, Carol: Frank's N3 Scout groups put Grace and Heidi in separate groups, which disproved Grace's claimed Medic visit to Heidi. Grace was the Jester.

entries.tip: A Seer SAME pair that includes a confirmed-Good player means the other player is Good or held the Katana that night. Don't dismiss it as untestable. Combine it with elimination (players confirmed by a flip or a self-proving action, players who survived or died to the Katana, your own role) to narrow down the holder.

support.note: Moderator: Carol's N4 pair Heidi/Judy matched. With Frank confirmed by his shot and Erin attacked, the holder had to be Judy, Grace or Carol. The town dismissed the pair and hanged Carol, the Seer; Judy then killed Erin. Carol and Heidi stressed the holder caveat.

entries.tip: In the final three or four, list who is confirmed Good (by mechanical results, a flip of the attacker, or your own role) and who died to or survived the Katana. Every unconfirmed living player is a possible holder; if only one is left, hang them. Don't let the last Yakuza reframe the vote as 'votes only, no mechanics', and don't fall back on old vote patterns when mechanics already narrow it.

support.note: Moderator and Carol: on D6 Grace reasoned that Frank was confirmed by his shot, she herself was Good, and Erin died to the Katana, so Judy had to be the holder. Judy's Jester/Executioner deflection failed, and she was hanged 2-1.

entries.tip: Before a hang, check who casts the deciding Guilty votes. A player named by the nominee's own result (e.g. their Seer pair) who rushes to vote Guilty on them gains the most if the result was true. Treat a nominee's mechanical case against a voter as a reason to scrutinize that vote, not to discount the result.

support.note: Erin and the moderator: Judy (Grunt, Katana) cast the deciding third Guilty on Carol right after Carol's pair pointed at her, then killed Erin that night.

entries.tip: Answer a direct question about your night action in one plain sentence the first time it is asked. Evasion repeated over days becomes a case of its own, even when the true answer is harmless.

support.note: Bob: his repeated evasion over two days about his night target became the case for nominating him.
Carol, Bob, Dave: hedged or flip-flopped answers about night actions (Heidi's, Bob's) were the main sources of wasted Days and of trials.
Bob and Heidi, plus the moderator's review: Bob's days of refusing a plain yes/no about visiting Erin became the central case and hanged him on D6.
Moderator: Erin's repeated non-answers about her night target got her nominated 9-2. A plain claim acquitted her 11-0.
Moderator (0.4), Dave, Carol, Mallory (0.16 each): Grace's slow answer to the N2 visit question nearly got the Vanilla hanged 4-5. Carol and Mallory (Yakuza) say plain early answers kept them safe.
Moderator, Ivan, Erin: Grace's 'I won't post my target' and Ivan's 'I won't explain' became the main leads against them.
Erin, Ivan, Grace: Heidi's dodged N5 visit question and Ivan's refusals to answer yes/no became the cases that hanged them.

entries.tip: Assume a freshly claimed investigator is both protected by the Medic and watched by a Lookout. Never send the Katana at a player a Lookout or Tracker has publicly said they will watch. Kill the watcher first, or hit someone else. A Katana holder sent straight at a watched target will be named as a visitor even if the attack fails, and a low-value holder with a Vanilla claim has no answer for that visit. Prefer an unclaimed or less obvious target, or a holder whose agreed public claim explains a visit there. Don't let the holder be the lone visitor to a victim while a Lookout may be alive.

support.note: Moderator, Erin, Ivan, Carol: N2 Ivan carried the Katana to claimed Sheriff Heidi (protected by Niaj, watched by Judy). N3 Carol went to claimed Seer Grace while Judy watched. Both holders were seen and hanged.

history.old: Assume a freshly claimed investigator is both protected by the Medic and watched by a Lookout. A Katana holder sent straight at them will be named as a visitor even if the attack fails, and a low-value holder with a Vanilla claim has no answer for that visit. Prefer an unclaimed or less obvious target, or a holder whose agreed public claim explains a visit there. Don't let the holder be the lone visitor to a victim while a Lookout may be alive.
history.note: Moderator, Heidi: Bob announced on D2 he would watch Judy on N2. Grace still Katana'd Judy, Bob named her as the only other visitor, and she was hanged D3.

entries.tip: An Ex-Con always reads Evil to alignment checks. A credible Not Evil Sheriff result on a player who later claims Ex-Con disproves the claim, and fits a Katana holder that night. Treat that combination as a concrete contradiction, all the more if the claim appeared only after the nomination.

support.note: Moderator, Heidi, Dave, Grace, Judy, Mallory, Frank: Ivan read Not Evil on N2 (he held the Katana), then claimed Ex-Con on trial. The town hanged him 10-1, and he flipped Grunt.

entries.tip: When a player flips Good but a Sheriff or Seer reported them Evil that night, read it first as a Fabricator frame, not as proof the investigator lied. A frame also means the victim's will may be forged, so don't act on that will's accusations. Re-derive any Seer pair that included the framed player, since the pair compares appearances. A DIFFERENT pair with no known alignment doesn't say which player is which.

support.note: Moderator, Heidi, Judy, Dave, Grace, Mallory: Heidi's N1 'Dave Evil' plus Dave's Tracker flip proved a frame. Dave's will was forged as 'Sheriff: Mallory Evil'. Grace corrected her Mallory pair reading, and framed Mallory was never mislynched.

entries.tip: Check every claimed neighbor-group result (Surveyor, Diviner, census-type group) against the circle as it stood at the start of that night. Remove the dead, skip the user's own seat, and walk both directions to the nearest eligible player. Write the steps out publicly. A group with the wrong neighbors exposes a fake claim at once, and it is a clean mechanical contradiction. But a wrong 'impossible' call puts a true investigator on trial and costs the accuser credibility the Yakuza will use later, so get the steps right before calling it.

support.note: Moderator, Alice, Bob, Dave, Heidi, Carol: Dave's skip-rule error sent Surveyor Carol to trial on D2. Grace later used the retraction against Dave.

history.old: Before calling a neighbor-group result (Surveyor, Diviner, census-type group) impossible, rebuild the circle as it stood at the start of that night. Remove the dead, skip the user's own seat, and walk both directions to the nearest eligible player. Write the steps out publicly. A wrong 'impossible' call puts a true investigator on trial and costs the accuser credibility the Yakuza will use later.
history.note: Moderator, Frank, Heidi, Dave, Bob, Alice, Mallory: Frank's fake Diviner N3 group Mallory/Ivan/Bob was broken by Grace's circle check (Mallory's living neighbors were Ivan and Alice), and he had to admit the lie. Adds the positive use to the earlier caution.

entries.tip: Killing the investigator whose public result already points at you doesn't erase it: their flip and will confirm the result for the town. If a posted result is already damning, plan the Day around it instead: prepare a counter-narrative, bus the exposed teammate, or spend a Day tool (puppet the main accuser). Spend the Katana on someone whose information isn't public yet.

support.note: Moderator and Frank: killing Census Taker Heidi on N2 made her flip and will confirm the census. Dave opened D3 by nominating Frank on exactly that basis.

entries.tip: Hanging one Yakuza doesn't stop the Katana: it passes to a random living teammate. Count how many Yakuza can still be alive, expect a kill the next night, and keep the same protective and watching plans in place.

support.note: Carol: after Erin, the holder, was hanged, Bob still had the Katana on N3 and Alice died.

entries.tip: Before every trial vote, compute the Guilty majority (strictly more than half of all votes counted) and how many votes would flip the result. A tie acquits. On a close trial of a strong suspect, a single Innocent from a Good voter on a technicality hands the Yakuza another night.

support.note: Ivan: Erin's 4-4 D2 trial acquitted her, and Heidi died that night. Two Good Innocent votes decided it.

entries.tip: When two players claim the same role whose actions were public (e.g. Prosecutor), compare their public reads from before each action with the actual targets: the real holder's reads predict the picks. Check labels too: night actions belong to nights (N2 for a Day 3 trial), and a claimant who uses the announcement days (D3/D4) is likely copying the public log. Before hanging the loser, list every way to assign the leftover roles: the copycat may be a Neutral claiming a power role to survive, and a player in another claim (e.g. a Unique Neutral) may be the real Yakuza.

support.note: Erin (Vulture) copied Ivan's Prosecutor claim with D3/D4 labels and had vouched for Dave; Ivan had named Dave and Niaj before each prosecution. Grace, Heidi, Carol, Mallory, Alice and the moderator. Alice and Grace: hanging the Neutral is what exposed Judy.

entries.tip: Give the Katana to the teammate who is already exposed and likely to be hanged next Day. A Lookout then only sees a player the town already suspects, and when they die the Katana passes to an unseen member with no visits against them. If the Mortician must clean, have him hold the Katana and clean his own kill, so only one Yakuza visits the victim; never stack a second Yakuza visitor on the target. The exposed holder may be blocked, so weigh that risk.

support.note: Dave held and cleaned Bob on N2, doomed Niaj killed Heidi on N3; Judy stayed unseen until the final four. Dave, Frank, Niaj and the moderator.

entries.tip: When a teammate's cover depends on a Neutral staying alive and unflipped (e.g. the teammate fake-claims that Neutral's Unique role), never push the Neutral's hang, and steer the town away from it. If that Neutral is in a claim duel with a villager, use the Katana on the villager side, so the town keeps an unopposed claimant and no flip touches your cover.

support.note: Judy claimed Vulture; the real Vulture Erin was hanged D5 in her Prosecutor duel and her flip exposed Judy. Judy, Niaj, Bob and the moderator.

entries.tip: When a Clerk may hold an unused rig, a passed nomination can be an execution, and an Innocent majority won't save anyone. Nominate your top suspect first, before they can nominate a Good player. If a player from a suspected pool opens the Day by nominating a claimed investigator or another likely Good player, vote No on the nomination itself. Never vote Yes 'so they can answer'. Publicly ask trusted players to do the same. A rig is announced only when the trial goes Innocent. The Clerk has one token, so once a rig fires it is spent.

support.note: Ivan's reflection on the rig risk in the D5-D6 endgame.

history.old: When a Clerk rig may be running, nominate your top suspect first, before they can nominate a Good player. Publicly ask trusted players to vote No on any nomination of a confirmed or likely Good player, since a passed nomination is an execution.
history.note: Moderator, Heidi, Dave: on D4 Bob (Clerk, in Heidi's Fabricator pool) nominated the claimed Surveyor Heidi first thing. Dave, Grace and Mallory voted Yes 'so she could answer', and the nomination passed 6-3. The trial went 5-4 Innocent, but the rig executed her.

entries.tip: When a teammate fake-claims an investigator, pick 'Evil' targets nobody can soon prove Good: not a likely Katana target, not a claimed Medic or Vanilla who may flip soon. Never spend the Katana on a player your fake Sheriff called Evil. Attacking them shows the Yakuza don't think they're Evil, and if they survive they have a confirmed story that breaks the claim.

support.note: Alice called Erin and Carol Evil. The Yakuza Katana'd Erin on N2, and she survived on self-protection. Carol then flipped Vanilla. Frank used 'Yakuza don't Katana their own' to hang Alice. Reported by the moderator, Alice and Ivan.

entries.tip: A survey, Diviner or other group result names a pool, not a holder. Before hanging one member, say what separates them from the others, and weigh how reliable that tiebreaker is. Framing can make any Good player read Evil for a night. An Evil check from an unverified Sheriff whose earlier Evil target was later shown Good (survived a Katana, flipped Vanilla) should count for almost nothing. If nothing reliable separates the pool, test a member that night rather than hang on a chain of conditionals.

support.note: On D3 the town hanged Vanilla Carol over Bob (Clerk) on Alice's framed 'Carol Evil'. Erin had already survived a Katana attack after Alice called her Evil. Reported by the moderator, Carol, Frank, Judy, Mallory and Dave.

entries.tip: Stay low-profile: give short, non-committal comments, vote with majorities, and don't attract checks. Douse players the town won't hang soon. A claimed Cardinal is an excellent douse: igniting them sets off a Divine curse on a random Good player, an extra kill that can clear the board.

support.note: Mallory doused Cardinal Dave on N1 and was never asked for a claim. On N5 the ignite killed Dave, Ivan and Judy, and Dave's curse took Frank, the last Good player. Reported by the moderator and Heidi.
Moderator: Mallory claimed Vanilla, voted with the town (Innocent on Heidi, nominated Alice) and was never seriously suspected while dousing over N1-N4.
Moderator: Mallory was never seriously suspected while dousing, and igniting the hidden Cardinal Dave triggered a curse that killed Frank.

entries.tip: The stall rule is a deadline for any death, and a night kill resets it too. It is not a reason to hang a particular suspect. When stall pressure comes up, say how many days and nights remain, and don't let it turn a pool result or a shaky check into a Guilty vote.

support.note: Dave and Mallory: stall-rule fear helped push the D3 mis-hang of Vanilla Carol on pool logic.

entries.tip: If an Arsonist may be alive (e.g. an archive lists one), hunt it as well as the Village. You can't see douses, and one ignite can kill your whole remaining team. Steer the town's suspicion toward quiet unclaimed players, and consider spending the Katana on the likeliest Arsonist rather than one more villager.

support.note: Ivan: the Yakuza ignored the archive-listed Arsonist, and Mallory's ignite killed Ivan, the last Yakuza.
Judy: the team had no plan for the living Arsonist, whose N4 ignite killed two Yakuza.
Bob and Carol: the Yakuza killed only info roles, while Arsonist Heidi's ignite killed two Yakuza and she went on to win.

entries.tip: If your target holds a well-verified Village role (e.g. an Archivist whose list checked out), don't push them directly; it only makes you suspect. Keep them alive and wait for an endgame where a mis-hang is plausible, or plan for your Jester fallback if they die another way.

support.note: Grace: her target was a verified Archivist, she never had a route to the hang, and she ended the game a Jester.

entries.tip: In a final four or five where a solo killer (e.g. an Arsonist) may be alive, count what each hang leaves behind before voting. Count the hang itself, a Jester's revenge on a Guilty voter and that night's kill. If they can leave you one against one with the killer, you lose: with two alive, a nomination needs both Yes votes, so the killer just votes No and kills you. Spend the late hangs on the likeliest killer, never on a likely Jester. If you must hang a possible Jester, keep the Guilty votes to a bare majority.

support.note: Moderator, Dave, Mallory: on D6 the town hanged Jester Grace 4-0. The revenge killed Carol, which left Dave alone with Arsonist Mallory, who blocked every nomination and ignited him.

Moderator: after a six-death N4, Vanilla Carol faced Ivan (Yakuza) and Mallory (Arsonist) at three alive. Hanging either one handed the game to the other. Identify every faction and count pending curses (Cardinal, Jester) before such a night.
Moderator: on D5 at 5 alive the town hanged Vanilla Dave, which left Bob, Heidi and Mallory. From there no hang could give the Village a win.
Moderator: at three alive Erin voted Guilty on Jester Frank. It handed him the win, and Bob killed her that night.
Moderator: hanging Ivan at four alive left a final three with the Jester holding the deciding vote, which lost the game; count what each late hang leaves behind.

entries.tip: A frame only changes alignment checks (Sheriff, Seer). Before framing, check whether a living alignment investigator is likely to check that player that night; otherwise the visit buys nothing and only adds your name to Lookout lists. Spend the forge on a night the target is the Katana's likely victim, or it dies with you.

support.note: Ivan: Alice's frames had no alignment checker to read them, and she died with her forge token unused.
Ivan: with no alignment checker alive, his frames bought nothing and his forge went unused.
Moderator and Ivan: Ivan framed Bob, Erin and Alice with no alignment checker in the game. Bob's watch on Erin saw the frame visit, which led to Ivan's hang.

entries.tip: Have a claim ready before Day 2 that explains your douse visits. Never deny acting, and never admit a vague 'I took an action elsewhere'. A Tracker cover that reports your real douse targets as 'tracks' fits Fortune Teller counts and Cartographer groups well and matches your 0 tokens. But if you denied acting earlier, that denial becomes the town's standing contradiction against you. Ex-Con explains random-looking visits and 0 tokens, but you read Not Evil to a Sheriff while an Ex-Con reads Evil. So use it only where no credible Sheriff result on you exists, and describe its automatic visit exactly. An Oracle guess breaks any cover, so pick one early and keep it. Spread douses across suspected Yakuza and key town roles.

support.note: Moderator: Mallory's D2 'action elsewhere' admission was a loose end nobody pulled. Her D5 Ex-Con claim then got Carol to spare her and hang Ivan with her.

history.old: Have a claim ready before Day 2 that explains your douse visits, and never admit a vague 'I took an action elsewhere'. Ex-Con explains random-looking visits and 0 tokens, but you read Not Evil to a Sheriff while an Ex-Con reads Evil. So use it only where no credible Sheriff result on you exists, and describe its automatic visit exactly. Spread douses across suspected Yakuza and key town roles.
history.note: Moderator: Heidi's douse targets presented as tracks fit Ivan's counts and Alice's group and won her the D4 acquittal. Her earlier no-action denial still hanged her on D7.

entries.tip: Don't use the puppet to post fake investigative results in a living investigator's name. They are told they were puppeted, and the next Day they post the real results. That proves a Puppeteer exists and makes their true results look stronger. Use the puppet for an effect that can't be undone the next Day, such as a damaging nomination or vote push, or a puppet the team will kill that night.

support.note: Moderator: Ivan posted a fake N2 Scout result as Frank. On D4 Frank posted his real groups and noted the puppeting in his will. That confirmed the archive's Puppeteer, and Frank's groups then drove the next hang.

entries.tip: When two surveys (or Diviner groups) both show the same role and the groups share one player, that player is the likeliest holder, not a proven one. Each result samples one random member, and roles can repeat. Weigh it as odds: unless the role is common, the shared player is far likelier than anyone else. Don't let 'not proof' acquit them; combine it with their claim, token count and votes, and hang if nothing better explains it.

support.note: Heidi's N1 and N3 surveys both showed Clerk and overlapped only on Bob. Bob, Dave, Judy, Mallory and Ivan correctly said it wasn't proof. But Bob was the Clerk and admitted it, and the moderator says the town should have hanged him on D4.

entries.tip: Before each vote, re-read your own private vote reminder and make sure your ballot matches the stance you just posted; say 'as of now' if you might change it. Ballots are secret, but announced totals are compared with stated votes. A stated Innocent that the totals show was Guilty puts everyone on that side under suspicion, and the town can hang a good player over it. If you slip, correct it publicly before the next nomination.

support.note: Mallory posted Innocent on Ivan and Heidi but voted Guilty both times. She was hanged on D6 as a Vanilla. Reported by the moderator, Carol, Dave, Erin, Ivan, Judy and Mallory (public-ballot game; reworded for totals-only settings).
Moderator: Grace (the nominator), Ivan, Judy and Dave said they leaned Guilty on Erin and then voted Innocent, which saved the Katana holder 2-7.

entries.tip: Post your two raw totals, labeled by night, in your first speech each Day from Day 2; don't hold them back. Keep your result and your deductions visibly separate: 'N2 totals: 4 and 4' is your result, and 'combined with X's and Y's claims, this means Z visited the victim' is a deduction from public claims. Never call a deduction 'private information'. A totals-only role can't name visitors, so unlabeled names read as night-chat knowledge.

support.note: Ivan withheld his numbers until D4, then called his deductions 'private Night 2 information' and was hanged as a true Fortune Teller. Reported by the moderator and Ivan.
Ivan and Mallory: posting the raw nightly numbers let the town cross-check the tracks and groups.
Ivan and the moderator: Ivan withheld his numbers for most of D4, was nominated 7-1, and was killed N4.
Heidi and Ivan: Heidi's counts pointed the right way but weren't lined up against claimed visits before she died N4, and no one could test them afterwards.
Mallory and Erin: Mallory stayed silent until D4, so her counts were never corroborated before the Katana killed her.

entries.tip: A fake visit-based result (Lookout, Tracker) about a victim your team attacked must leave room for a killer other than you. Never name, as the victim's only other visitor, someone who can't be the holder (a declared Neutral, a confirmed townie). That leaves you as the only possible attacker, and a mapper or watcher finishes it. If a Cartographer has announced map tokens or a Lookout or Tracker is active, pass the Katana to an unexposed member that night or have the Smuggler swap the holder. Prefer a cover with no checkable visits.

support.note: Bob killed Oracle Carol on N2 while Cartographer Alice mapped him. He then claimed Lookout with declared-Neutral Heidi as the only other visitor and was hanged 9-1 on D3; his own teammates had to agree. The swaps and a Katana pass went unused. Reported by the moderator, Frank and Bob.

entries.tip: Spend your swap tokens on the nights they protect the team: when a Cartographer, Lookout or Tracker is likely to catch the Katana holder, when a Vigilante shot or trap may hit a teammate, or to redirect a kill onto a protected target's neighbor. Swapping the holder with a non-Yakuza moves actions aimed at the holder, so plan it in night chat. Tokens still unused at 2-3 Yakuza alive are usually wasted.

support.note: Frank held both swap tokens all 7 Days. A swap on N2, when Alice openly mapped Bob, could have saved him. Reported by Frank, Judy and the moderator.
Moderator: Frank held both swaps all game and died to the N4 ignite while holding the Katana.
Frank and the moderator: both swap tokens went unused while Alice's map exposed the holder Bob. Frank died to the ignite still holding them.
Moderator: Carol never used either swap, even though a swap could have redirected Frank's audit or Judy's watch. She was hanged holding both.

Carol held both swaps unused. A swap moves every action aimed at either player, so to beat a Medic, aim the Katana at the swap partner and swap them with the protected target. Plan it before the night.
Moderator (0.4) and Bob (0.16): Bob died holding both swap tokens. A swap could have moved Frank's protection or Heidi's N3 check.
Frank, Erin: Frank held both swap tokens for the whole game. Use them to redirect a known protection.

entries.tip: Post your nightly group sizes in your first speech every Day, and post a map result (named group) as soon as you have it, before the mapped player's visit claim is tested. A map in your will after you die comes too late. Don't announce whom you'll map or how many map tokens you have left: it tells the Yakuza to move the Katana, swap, or kill you. A group shows who is linked, not who visited whom, so pair it with a Lookout or Tracker report before naming a holder.

support.note: Alice's N2 map on Bob showed a group that his Lookout claim couldn't square, but she posted it only after dying. She had openly announced her map tokens. Reported by Alice and the moderator.
Alice: post the group sizes and named groups early, before you die.

entries.tip: Cartographer and Scout groups are undirected. A Katana kill puts the holder in the victim's group that night, but the group alone doesn't say who attacked whom. First narrow the holder to the group's members. Then eliminate: remove the victim, any member confirmed as no-action (by a flip or an Oracle RIGHT on Vanilla) whose link the victim's own visit can explain, and any member with a corroborated harmless visit. If only one unconfirmed member is left, treat them as the likely holder and act that Day, especially if they dodge a plain yes/no about their own visit. 'A link isn't a visit' and 'test it from outside the group first' must not acquit that last member. Use a direction-aware result (Lookout, Tracker) only when elimination doesn't finish the job.

support.note: Alice and Bob: the group linking Bob, Carol and Heidi didn't pin the holder by itself; Bob's own Lookout claim did.

history.old: Cartographer and Scout groups are undirected. A Katana kill puts the holder in the victim's group that night, but the group doesn't say who attacked whom. Use a group to narrow the holder to its members, then separate them with a direction-aware result (Lookout, Tracker) or the members' own claims.
history.note: Moderator: Alice's N2 map showed Bob, Dave and Erin. Dave was a true Vanilla (Carol's Oracle hit) and Erin had audited Dave, so Bob had to be the holder. Dave, Grace, Mallory, Heidi and Ivan all repeated 'a group is only a link', Bob was acquitted 1-7, and he went on to kill Ivan and Grace.

entries.tip: When a claimed check is posted without the exact role guessed, the target and the night, ask once, plainly, for all three before voting. Don't vote on a bare 'X is not a Tracker', but don't throw it away either. An evasive real investigator is still an investigator, so weigh the full result once it is given. Discount a check that first appears only after its author is nominated.

support.note: Dave, Grace, Mallory, Heidi, Alice, Bob: Carol's unnamed N4 result drove two trials and a Vigilante push. The moderator adds that it was true and the town wrongly discounted it.

entries.tip: Know which actions are Astral: Oracle and Ritualist guesses, the Arsonist's ignite and the Cartographer's map. No Lookout, Tracker, Fortune Teller, trap, Veteran or Katana holder can see or react to them. 'My target would be exposed' is never a reason to withhold an Astral result. Yakuza: an Oracle isn't a visit-reader. Rank Trackers, Lookouts, Fortune Tellers and Cartographers as the visit threats, and the Oracle as an exact-role threat.

support.note: Bob and Frank: Bob wanted to kill Carol as a 'visit-reader', and Carol's 'exposure' excuse for an Astral guess was called out by the moderator.

entries.tip: State your reason in the same message as every nomination, and if you drop a push, say why. An unexplained nomination becomes a lasting lever against you, even when the target was right. If someone else's nomination has no reason, ask for it once and weigh the answer against checkable results rather than repeating the pressure.

support.note: Frank, Dave, Alice and the moderator: Carol's unexplained D3 nomination of Bob, who was Yakuza, was used against her for three Days and helped hang her.

entries.tip: Speaking budget is limited, and late-round messages cost more. Ask a concrete question once, by name, and repeat it only when something changes. Save budget for your trial defense and for the late rounds when votes are decided.

support.note: Bob and Ivan: repeated long public demands for the same answer burned budget and added nothing.
Dave, Ivan, Judy: repeated 'no nomination' lines every round burned budget needed for trials.
Alice and Judy: repeated self-nominations and long pushes burned budget, and trial arguments ran short late in the Day.

Moderator (0.4), Bob, Frank (0.16 each): D1-D2 were filled with 'no nomination from me' posts. On D3 Heidi couldn't afford to answer a visit question, and on D5 Grace and Mallory were locked out of public speech by round 7.
Ivan: dozens of repeated 'no nomination without a mechanical lead' posts burned budget and added nothing.
Alice and Mallory: repeated questions, 'nothing new' posts and identical self-nominations burned budget for days without moving votes.
Bob, Carol, Heidi: repeated 'no nomination from me yet' and repeated yes/no demands burned budget without adding information.
Moderator, Bob, Heidi, Ivan, Judy: repeated 'name the night' and 'Grace, name the hit' demands burned budget for rounds while nobody analyzed the archive list.

entries.tip: Reconcile visit counts every night (Fortune Teller totals, Cartographer sizes, Scout groups) against all claimed and known visits. If an extra visitor/visited pair keeps showing up night after night and no living claimant explains it, a hidden actor is visiting, most often an Arsonist dousing or a Neutral killer. Ask unclaimed and Vanilla claimants for night accounts, and point a Lookout or Tracker at them. Treat the gap as a lead about a hidden visitor, not as proof the counter is lying.

support.note: Moderator: Alice's sizes showed a 2-player group every night and Ivan's N3 numbers were 2,2, both from Heidi dousing Frank, Ivan and Judy. Instead Judy, Frank and Bob called Ivan's numbers 'unsupported' and nominated him. Heidi ignited N4 and won.

entries.tip: Plan your endgame around votes. After a big ignite, vote to hang the last likely Yakuza rather than a Villager who can't kill you, and steer toward a final two with a non-killer. With two alive, a nomination needs both Yes votes, so they can't hang you and you ignite them. Stay non-committal by day so neither side targets you first.

support.note: Moderator: Heidi ignited on N4 (killing Frank, Ivan and Judy), helped hang Vanilla Dave on D5, voted Guilty on Bob on D6, then ignited Mallory to win.

entries.tip: When no credible Medic is protecting claimants, expect the Katana on every new power-role claimant that same night. Make your claim count: post every result at once with night, exact target and exact result, and write the exact targets in your will (e.g. 'N2: audited Dave, 0 tokens', not 'did a token check'). A vague will leaves links the Yakuza can exploit after you die.

support.note: Moderator, Grace, Erin, Carol: Carol, Erin, Alice and Ivan were each killed the night after claiming or being exposed. Erin's will didn't name Dave as her audit target, which let Bob argue her audit might explain his own link.
Moderator: with no Medic, every investigator who claimed died the next night.
Moderator (0.4) and Frank (0.16): with no Medic, claimed FT Frank died N2 and claimed Accountant Grace died N3, each the night after claiming.

entries.tip: Use the Night 1 Katana attack. In a large town with many unclaimed investigators, a skipped kill lets every power role reach Day 2, claim and cross-check results. That shared picture corners your team fast. Kill a likely investigator or organizer on N1 unless there's a concrete reason to wait (e.g. several investigators are certain to land on your holder).

support.note: Moderator: the Yakuza skipped N1. On D2 the Lookout, Tracker, Seer, Archivist and Oracle all claimed and confirmed one another, and all three Yakuza were hanged by D4.
Moderator: the Yakuza wasted N1. Only the Jester hang made it irrelevant.
Ivan: skipping the N1 kill cost tempo with nothing gained, and gave the Village time to build visit lists.

entries.tip: The first time you're pressed for your night target, claim Ex-Con in one plain sentence. Say you visit a random player every night, aren't told whom, and read Evil to alignment checks. That explains a missing target, any Lookout or Tracker sighting of you at a victim, and a DIFFERENT Seer pair or Evil result. Evasive 'I can't name a target' answers build a case for your trial.

support.note: Moderator and Erin: Erin dodged for five rounds and was nominated 9-2. Once she claimed Ex-Con on trial, the claim fit Judy's pair and the archive, and she was acquitted 11-0.

entries.tip: Use your block every night. Decide the target in night chat before Day 2 settles. Good targets are a claimed Seer or Lookout whose next result could expose the team, or the likely Medic on a kill night. An unused block is a free night for the town's investigators.

support.note: Ivan never blocked anyone all game. The Seer, Lookout, Tracker and Oracle all acted freely and their results cornered the team.
Bob, Ivan, Carol: Ivan's nightly blocks on Dave, Mallory and Alice stopped the Lookout, Oracle and Prosecutor while the Katana struck elsewhere.

entries.tip: A player who publicly claims a role that exists only on the Yakuza side (Grunt, Clerk, Diviner, Pharmacist, Puppeteer, Ritualist, etc.) has given you the strongest lead you will get. This holds even if they label it '(Village)' and withdraw it as a typo once called out, and above all when a public archive lists that role and nobody else claims it. Learn which faction every role belongs to, and check each claimed role against that list. Treat such a claim as a confession, not a wording slip. Accurate results don't clear it. Evil investigators like the Diviner get true information, and a player confirming one of their hits (e.g. a Vigilante confirming the drawn role) authenticates that result, not the claimant. 'It was a slip, show me a mechanical result' must not shield them. Nominate and hang them while the Village still has the numbers, and if you said you lean Guilty, vote Guilty.

history.note: Moderator: Alice openly claimed Diviner on D2 and posted accurate groups. Carol's Vigilante confirmation made her 'gain weight', nobody noticed Diviner is Yakuza-only, and the Katana holder steered three Days.

entries.tip: Report only what your role actually saw, and label everything else as a deduction from public claims (e.g. 'from Judy's and Frank's posts, X visited Y'). A Medic sees only her own protection, a Lookout only her target's visitors. A visit list your role can't produce costs you credibility for days, even when it's right. Village: ask once for the source of any full-night visit list before using it, and treat an unsourced one as the claimant's mistake to explain, not as evidence.

support.note: Moderator, Carol, Dave, Frank, Grace, Heidi, Ivan, Judy: Medic Alice posted a full N1 visit list she couldn't have seen, retracted it, and was doubted for two days.

entries.tip: A nonzero token count on a player claiming a tokenless role (Vanilla, Grunt, Jester, Executioner, Serial Killer, Arsonist, Ex-Con) is a hard contradiction. A Philanthropist can't explain it: a gift to a role without tokens is thrown away and isn't counted. Only a token role can explain the count. Name the count, the claim it breaks and the roles it fits in one message before the vote.

support.note: Frank's 1-token audit on 'Vanilla' Mallory and 2 on 'Vanilla' Carol. Some players raised Philanthropist gifts as an excuse, which the rules rule out for tokenless roles. Both were Yakuza.

entries.tip: When a strong suspect is nominated, even by someone you distrust or by a possible teammate, vote Yes if you hold any real lead (a self-incriminating slip, slot math, an Evil result). Passing a nomination only opens a trial, and you still decide at the trial. A No on a strong suspect's nomination wastes the chance, and while the Village still holds the numbers it hands the Yakuza a free night. Exception: if a Clerk may hold an unused rig, a passed nomination can mean an execution (see t38/t199).

support.note: Moderator: on D3 Carol nominated her own teammate Erin. Grace, Heidi, Ivan and Alice voted No, and it failed with 3 Yes. With their votes it would have passed 7, and a Village-majority trial could have hanged the Katana holder.
Moderator: on D6, Erin's No left Frank's nomination of Grace one Yes short. Frank, Erin and Jester Judy could have passed it and hanged her.

entries.tip: Stay visibly and moderately active by day: post short, concrete reads on other players' claims and results. Long role silence from several players makes them the town's 'unclaimed pool' once a role list exists. Silent players who then vote together on a trial form a bloc the town can read. Spread your votes so teammates aren't the only ones pushing a trial.

support.note: Mallory and Grace: Carol and Mallory stayed unclaimed until D5 and drew silence-based nomination threats. Their joint D6 Guilty votes on Dave formed a readable bloc.
Moderator: Erin, Frank and Judy echoed the Village's own reasoning, joined the crowd hangs of Ivan, Alice and Grace, and were never seriously suspected.

entries.tip: If you hold an exact-role result showing that a nominee is a Jester (an Oracle RIGHT, a survey or archive slot that pins them), post it in full (night, target, exact role, result) before the nomination vote, or at the latest at the start of the trial. Voting Innocent while hinting 'a hanged Jester wins' changes no votes. Revealing your role costs far less than what the hang costs: the Jester's win, a revenge kill on a Guilty voter, and a second revenge kill if an Executioner targeting them also wins.

support.note: Moderator: Carol's N1 Oracle guess confirmed Judy as Jester, but she only voted Innocent with a vague hint. Judy was hanged 10-1, Executioner Dave won too, and the two revenge attacks killed Erin and Mallory.
Moderator: Carol posted her Jester RIGHT on Judy on D2, and later her Executioner read on Dave. Every nomination of either failed, so neither won and no revenge fired.

entries.tip: Count the full cost of a likely-Jester hang before voting. The revenge Divine-attacks a random Guilty voter the next night. If an Executioner whose target was that player also wins on the hang, they leave and a second random Guilty voter dies. Add the Katana kill that same night and one Day can remove four Village players and hand the Yakuza half the table, after which no Village nomination can pass. Keep Guilty votes to a bare majority, with confirmed power roles voting Innocent.

support.note: Moderator: Judy (Jester, also Dave's Executioner target) was hanged 10-1. Dave left, both revenges killed Erin and Mallory, and the Katana killed Alice, taking the board from 11 to 6 with 3 Yakuza.

entries.tip: Make vote pushes in public, not by private message. A PM asking for a Yes before a second source exists is visible to everyone as a trail, and opponents reframe it as a 'whip' to put you on trial. Post the evidence publicly and let the votes follow. Village: an honest player PMing for votes on a credible result (e.g. a Lookout log) is pushing clumsily, not proving a bloc. Judge the result they pushed, not the PMs.

support.note: Alice, Bob, Erin, Frank, Mallory: Frank's PMs asking for Yes votes on Grace (backed by Bob's true Lookout log) were turned into a 'whip' case, and the Yakuza hanged Vanilla Frank on D4.

entries.tip: When a villager privately lobbies for votes against a teammate, don't defend the teammate on the evidence. Nominate the lobbyist publicly, citing their visible PM trail as vote-steering. Near parity this can hang them, and it moves the Day's topic off your teammate.

support.note: Ivan: Grace nominated Frank over his PMs asking for Yes votes on her, and the Yakuza hanged him 3-2 on D4.

entries.tip: Don't let an obvious Jester's self-nominations eat the Day. Each passed nomination uses one of the three trial slots, so vote No on a repeat self-nomination unless something new supports it. Agree early that a repeat nomination needs a new result. Sparing the Jester is not a reason to skip the day's hang: spend the Day's trials on the strongest Yakuza case (a count, a log, a refused night account). Exception: in a final three with the Jester holding the deciding vote, see t181.

support.note: Moderator (0.4): on D6, Erin and Frank voted Yes on Judy's self-nomination, and two of the three trials went to her while holder Grace survived. Alice, Frank, Mallory and Erin (0.16 each) said repeated self-nominations drained about four Days.

entries.tip: Don't fake an Evil investigative result against a player who may really be Yakuza. If the read is true, the Yakuza kill you that night, and a Jester killed at night wins nothing. Prefer a fake claim that invites your hang without threatening the Yakuza, e.g. a shaky result on a likely townie, or a weak claim you then defend badly. Once an exact-role check has outed you, stop self-nominating: the town won't pass it, and repeats only burn budget.

support.note: Moderator: Judy's fake 'Sheriff: Ivan Evil' was accidentally true, and the Katana killed her N2. Dave self-nominated seven times after Carol outed him and never got more than 2 Yes votes.

entries.tip: Spend the Day's three trials purposefully. Nominate only someone you'd vote Guilty on if their answer fails, and state the test before nominating. A trial nobody intends to convict uses up a slot, reveals nothing and can end the Day without a hang. Keep a public count of the R14 stall clock (quiet Nights and Days since the last death), and when deaths stop, push for a real test or a mechanical nomination early in the Day.

support.note: Moderator (0.4): on D3 Bob, Carol and Frank were each tried and acquitted 0-8, ending the Day with no information. Carol and Frank (0.16 each) warned that stalling with unanimous Innocents pushed the game toward the stall rule.

entries.tip: Under secret ballots, stated votes alone prove nothing: Evil players can announce Innocent and vote Guilty, or split their stated votes to look independent. At small counts, though, the totals can catch the liar. If 3 of 4 voted Guilty and the nominee surely voted Innocent, everyone else who said Innocent lied. Do this arithmetic after every small trial, publicly name who must have lied, and make that player the next hang.

support.note: Moderator: on D5 Erin said she would vote Innocent on Bob and Heidi said Guilty. The trial still went 3 of 4 Guilty, which exposed Erin's lie, but the split made the two Yakuza look independent going into the final night.
Carol, moderator: the totals revealed Judy's hidden Guilty. Bob and Heidi caution that arithmetic resting on assumed votes is only a question to ask, not grounds for an accusation.

entries.tip: A Profiler's two decoy roles are drawn from the roles of other players alive at the start of that night (all roles only if too few are in play), so each decoy is almost always a real role among the living. The Profiler's own role is never drawn. Post the full three-role list and write it into your will the same Day. A Yakuza-only decoy (Clerk, Wiretap, Pharmacist, Smuggler, Ritualist) means that role is held by a living player: match it to suspects and unclaimed players, e.g. a player who quoted a PM plus a Wiretap decoy. Cross every profile with deaths and confirmed claims to strike options. Spend tokens on unclaimed players or on claims that conflict with a visit result, whose role would decide a vote. Don't re-profile an active claimant to confirm them, since one profile never confirms a claim.

support.note: Moderator (0.4): Carol's N3 profile of Vanilla Frank listed Clerk and Wiretap as decoys, nearly proving Erin (who had quoted a PM) was the Wiretap. Nobody used it, Carol was hanged, and the Yakuza won. Carol (0.16): combine profiles with deaths to eliminate options.

entries.tip: When a player quotes or closely paraphrases a private message they weren't party to, only an Eavesdropper (who visited the sender or receiver the night before) or the Yakuza Wiretap could have read it. Ask at once which role, and which player they eavesdropped. The named target must be in that exchange, and the visit must fit any Lookout, Tracker or visit-count data. A claim that can't name a fitting target, or a role list or profile decoy showing Wiretap, points to the Wiretap. Don't vote on the quoted PM's content until the quoter's access is explained.

support.note: Moderator (0.4), Alice, Carol, Heidi, Frank (0.16 each): Erin quoted Heidi's PM to Carol almost verbatim, and four players flagged it. Her untested Eavesdropper claim survived, the town never checked it against Carol's Wiretap decoy, and Erin won.

entries.tip: You can't be role-blocked, and a Village blocker whose block on you fails is told it failed on immunity. Party Animals test claimed Vanillas this way. Don't hide behind Vanilla. Before Day 2, agree in night chat on a cover that explains immunity, 0 tokens and a visit each night. Party Animal fits all three, but only while no real Party Animal has claimed or posted blocks. Never name your real role, even loosely ('Pharmacist-type'). Each block you land is told to its target. If a claimed investigator posts a block notice and no Village blocker claims it, the block points at your team. So block a claimed Tracker only when the night's stakes justify it.

support.note: Moderator, Erin, Frank: Erin's role slip plus Vanilla claim, Grace's failed N2 block on her and Bob's unexplained N2 block notice hanged her 7-3 on D3.

entries.tip: When roles stay hidden on death, use the night kill list as a claim test. A claimed investigator killed by the Katana was probably real, because the Yakuza kill the threats they can't explain away. In a duplicate claim, the rival who survives deserves the test (audit, exact-role check, watch). Weigh it against the possibility that the Yakuza killed a real townie to leave a fake standing, and act on it before the next night rather than after.

support.note: Alice and Grace (0.16 each): real Lookout Bob was the Katana kill after the D2 duplicate-claim fight. Archivist Carol and Vigilante Heidi died later the same way.

entries.tip: With quiet play, you can win without using any role token: no daytime teammate PMs, unanimous Katana votes, a kill on an information role every night, and votes that echo the town's own arguments. Let the Village spend its hangs on Neutrals, Roleplayers and duplicate-claim fights. Never lead a push, and keep 'no role claim' answers short and calm. Still agree one contingency per Day in night chat for when a teammate is nominated.

support.note: Moderator (0.4) and Erin (0.16): Erin, Frank and Judy used no abilities, killed Bob, Carol and Heidi, joined the Ivan, Alice and Grace hangs and won without ever being nominated. Erin noted they had no reserve plan at 5 alive.
